item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union MoS Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Inaugurates Modernised Jan Seva Connect Post Offices in Guntur
₹5,785-Crore Digital Transformation, AI-Powered Operations and Corporate Reforms Propel India Post into a New Era
Andhra Pradesh Postal Circle Emerges as the Nation's Best Performer in Q1 FY 2026–27
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, today inaugurated the modernised Kothapeta and Chandramouli Nagar Sub-Post Offices in Guntur under the 'Jan Seva Connect' initiative. Designed as next-generation citizen service centres, the renovated post offices combine modern infrastructure with the rich cultural heritage of Andhra Pradesh, offering integrated postal, banking, digital and logistics services under one roof.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Chandrasekhar said that India Post is no longer merely a department that delivers letters but a national institution connecting lives, empowering communities and driving India's digital and economic transformation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, the Department of Posts is undergoing the most comprehensive transformation in its 170-year history, positioning itself as a world-class logistics, e-commerce and financial services network.

The Minister of State said the Government has launched one of the country's largest technology modernisation programmes in the postal sector with an investment of ₹5,785 crore under IT 2.0 and Advanced Postal Technology (APT) 2.0. The initiative is integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud-based platforms and real-time data across the country's network of more than 1.65 lakh post offices, nearly 90 per cent of which are located in rural India. The transformation is enabling faster service delivery, real-time tracking, improved operational efficiency and a seamless customer experience.

Dr. Chandrasekhar said India Post has also embraced a corporate-style governance model by introducing strategic leadership positions such as Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) and Vice CTO. With clearly defined business targets, monthly performance reviews, accountability frameworks and a customer-first approach, the Department is becoming more agile, competitive and responsive to the evolving needs of citizens and businesses.

Highlighting the transformation in logistics, the Minister of State said India Post has introduced revised pricing, bulk discounts, Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) facilities, special packaging solutions, geotagged deliveries, SMS tracking, OTP-based delivery confirmation and 24-to-48-hour delivery standards. Strategic partnerships with ONDC, GeM, Amazon, Flipkart, Patanjali and international logistics providers such as DHL are significantly expanding India's e-commerce ecosystem and strengthening India Post's position in the logistics market.

He said post offices are rapidly evolving into integrated citizen service centres by offering UPI payments, Aadhaar enrolment and updation services, Passport Seva facilities, India Post Payments Bank doorstep banking, Postal Life Insurance, Rural Postal Life Insurance and government-backed savings schemes. India Post currently manages over 3.8 crore Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana accounts, while more than 60 per cent of postal transactions are now conducted digitally, reflecting the Department's successful transition towards a cash-lite, technology-enabled ecosystem.

The Minister of State described Gramin Dak Sevaks (GDS) and postmen as the backbone of this transformation. Through GDS Sammelans, structured training programmes, sales orientation, digital capacity building, grievance monitoring, recognition mechanisms and performance-linked accountability, India Post is empowering its frontline workforce to become trusted ambassadors of financial inclusion and digital governance in rural India. He said GDS employees are playing a crucial role in helping families understand savings, insurance and financial planning while expanding access to government services.

Dr. Chandrasekhar noted that these reforms are already producing remarkable results. During the first quarter of FY 2026–27, India Post recorded its highest-ever first-quarter revenue of over ₹4,000 crore, reaching ₹4,009 crore and registering a 22 per cent year-on-year growth. Zero-transaction accounts have declined by more than 90 per cent, while the Effective Capability Ratio (ECR) has improved from 41 per cent to 47 per cent, reflecting significant gains in operational efficiency.

Congratulating the Andhra Pradesh Postal Circle, the MoS said the Circle has emerged as the best-performing Postal Circle in the country during the first quarter of FY 2026–27. Andhra Pradesh achieved 102 per cent of its quarterly business target, generating ₹233.7 crore in revenue, secured the No. 1 national ranking in Mail Operations, recorded an impressive 140 per cent growth in parcel business, and generated over ₹50 crore under the 'Jayaho Bheema Sankalp' insurance campaign. He also noted that nearly 33 per cent of the beneficiary payments under major Andhra Pradesh Government welfare schemes, including Talliki Vandanam, Deepam, NTR Rythu Bharosa and NTR Nagar, are being delivered through the postal network, highlighting its unmatched last-mile reach.

Speaking about the Guntur projects, Dr. Chandrasekhar said the two post offices have been redesigned under the guidance of the School of Planning and Architecture to celebrate Andhra Pradesh's cultural identity. The Kothapeta Sub-Post Office, modernised at a cost of ₹51.81 lakh, features a distinctive red feature wall inspired by the 1975 Kuchipudi commemorative postage stamp, while the Chandramouli Nagar Sub-Post Office, renovated at a cost of ₹64.13 lakh, draws architectural inspiration from the iconic Ananda Nilayam tower of Tirumala.

The Minister of State congratulated the officers and staff of the Andhra Pradesh Postal Circle and Guntur Division for successfully implementing the Jan Seva Connect initiative. He conveyed special appreciation to the postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks, describing them as the real heroes behind India Post's success for delivering essential services to every household, irrespective of weather or geography.

Concluding his address, Dr. Chandrasekhar said that Viksit Bharat is not merely a Government mission but a shared national responsibility. He reaffirmed that the Centre and the Andhra Pradesh Government are working in close partnership to ensure faster, technology-driven and citizen-centric governance. He expressed confidence that every post office under the Jan Seva Connect initiative would emerge as a trusted public institution supporting students, empowering entrepreneurs, serving women, assisting senior citizens and strengthening communities while taking India another step closer to the vision of a Developed India.

"The Postal Department is not just about carrying letters—it is a bridge that connects millions of lives and reaches every corner of our state."

Inaugurated the newly renovated Kothapeta Sub-Post Office today alongside Guntur East MLA Shri Mohammed Naseer Ahmed .

item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Ayushman Arogya Shivir Concludes Successfully Across Three Kartavya Bhawans in New Delhi Over 1700 Government Officials and Staff from Over 16 Ministries Avail Preventive Health Screening and Medical Consultation Ni-kshay Vahans Equipped with Advanced Diagnostic Facilities Enable On-site TB Screening and Early Detection Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare successfully organised a three-day Ayushman Arogya Shivir from 22 to 24 July 2026 across Kartavya Bhawan-I, Kartavya Bhawan-II…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ayushman Arogya Shivir Concludes Successfully Across Three Kartavya Bhawans in New Delhi
Over 1700 Government Officials and Staff from Over 16 Ministries Avail Preventive Health Screening and Medical Consultation
Ni-kshay Vahans Equipped with Advanced Diagnostic Facilities Enable On-site TB Screening and Early Detection
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare successfully organised a three-day Ayushman Arogya Shivir from 22 to 24 July 2026 across Kartavya Bhawan-I, Kartavya Bhawan-II and Kartavya Bhawan-III in New Delhi. Organised by the Central TB Division (CTD) in collaboration with the Delhi State TB Cell, National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) and Swasth Nagrik Abhiyaan (SNA) Division of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the initiative aimed to promote preventive healthcare, facilitate early diagnosis and strengthen awareness on healthy living among Government officials and Central Secretariat staff working in the Kartavya Bhawans.

The Ayushman Arogya Shivir commenced at Kartavya Bhawan-I on 22nd July 2026, where it was inaugurated by Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. During the inauguration, she emphasised the importance of prioritising preventive healthcare and encouraging individuals to take proactive steps towards their health and well-being. The health camp was subsequently organised at Kartavya Bhawan-II on 23rd July, where Dr. Shobini Rajan, Deputy Director General, Central TB Division, interacted with participants and highlighted the importance of early detection, timely diagnosis and preventive healthcare in achieving the vision of a TB Mukt Bharat. The Shivir culminated at Kartavya Bhawan-III on 24th July 2026, ensuring wider outreach among Government officials and employees across the three office complexes.

The three-day initiative witnessed an encouraging response, with over 1700 Government officials and other staff from over 16 Ministries availing free health screening and medical consultation services. Comprehensive health assessments included Blood Pressure (BP) measurement, blood sugar testing, Body Mass Index (BMI) assessment, Haemoglobin (Hb) estimation, Chest X-ray screening, medical consultation and referral services, wherever required. Officers, security personnel, housekeeping staff, sanitation workers and other employees actively participated in the health camp, reaffirming the growing emphasis on preventive healthcare in the workplace.

A major highlight of the Shivir was the deployment of two Ni-kshay Vahans equipped with Digital Chest X-ray, CBNAAT and TrueNat diagnostic facilities. These mobile diagnostic units enabled on-site TB screening, molecular testing and prompt referral of suspected cases, thereby strengthening efforts towards early detection and timely treatment under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP).

The successful organisation of the health camp was supported by a dedicated team of around 60 healthcare providers, including doctors, specialists, laboratory personnel, radiographers, nursing staff, programme officials, TB Vijetas and My Bharat Volunteers, whose coordinated efforts ensured seamless delivery of healthcare services and effective awareness generation throughout the three-day initiative.

The Ayushman Arogya Shivir reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare, promoting early diagnosis and expanding access to quality health services. Such workplace-based initiatives contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat, Healthy India and TB Mukt Bharat by encouraging regular health check-ups, fostering health-seeking behaviour and facilitating early identification and treatment of diseases among Government employees.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PROMOTION OF AI USE IN AGRICULTURE AND IMPACT ASSESSMENT
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has initiated several AI-related projects. These are being used for farmer advisories, pest control, crop identification, insurance, delivery of scheme benefits, and governance analytics. Under the Digital Agriculture Mission, the Government also supports the States for projects involving modern digital technology, such as Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Block chain Technology, the Internet of Things, Robotics, etc. Some key AI initiatives of the government are as follows:

  1. National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS) – This system tackles the loss of produce due to climate change, utilizes AI and Machine Learning to detect pest infestation in crop issues, enabling timely intervention for healthier crops. This tool, currently used by over 10,000 extension workers, allows farmers to capture images of pests to help them mitigate pest attacks and reduce crop losses. At present, it supports 73 crops over 436 pests.
  2. AI-based Monsoon and Weather Advisory: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) provides AI-based monsoon and weather advisories to support informed agricultural decision-making. The advisories enable farmers to plan agricultural operations based on timely and location-specific weather forecasts. As on date, the initiative has reached approximately 5.28 crore farmers.
  3. BharatVistaar (Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources) is a multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture. The platform provides farmers with AI-enabled, real-time and location-specific agricultural advisories and access to Government schemes and agricultural support services.

As on date, the platform has served over 3 lakh farmers and addressed more than 72 lakh farmer queries. It provides information on 18 Central Government schemes, crop and livestock advisories, weather forecasts, mandi prices, pest and disease identification, soil health-based recommendations and grievance redressal.

The platform is available through a web portal, mobile application, AI chatbot and dedicated telephone line. At present, BharatVistaar Telephone service is available in 2 languages, i.e. Hindi and English; however, the chatbot, web portal, and mobile application are available in 10 languages.

 

No specific assessment has been undertaken by the Government to comprehensively evaluate the impact of AI-based technologies. The funds allocated and utilised for digital agriculture initiatives, including AI-based agricultural initiatives, during the last five years are as under:

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ROLLOUT OF WEATHER INFORMATION NETWORK DATA SYSTEM
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

Weather Information Network and Data System (WINDS) is an initiative of Government aimed at developing a national level network of Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) and Automatic Rain Gauges (ARGs) for generation of long term hyperlocal weather data for crop insurance, agriculture advisories and disaster risk resilience needs of different sectors. WINDS has been adopted by 7 States/UTs (Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha, Puducherry, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand) wherein as on date, 16,843 sites have been approved for installation, civil work has been completed in 1,188 site and 892 AWS/ ARGs have been installed.    

The PMFBY envisages adoption of improved technology in implementation of the scheme. Accordingly, Yield Estimation System based on Technology (YES-TECH) is being implemented with effect from Kharif 2023 for objective crop damage, loss assessment. YES-TECH envisages gradual migration to remote sensing based yield estimation to help in fair and accurate crop yield estimation. The initiative has been launched for paddy and wheat crops wef Kharif 2023 and for Soybean crop wef Kharif 2024 season wherein mandatory 30% weightage to yield estimation has been assigned to YES-TECH derived yield.

YES-TECH was implemented in 12 States across 344 Districts in 2025-26. Further, State Government of Madhya Pradesh has given 100% weightage to technology based yield, whereas State Governments of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh has given 50% weightage while Odisha and Karnataka State Governments have given 40% weightage to YES-TECH based yield in 2025-26.

Government has a mechanism of rigorous review with stakeholders on effective YES-TECH implementation.

Following steps have been taken by Govt. of India to for timely settlement of claims under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana:

  • Government has undertaken development of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) as a single source of data for subsidy payment, dissemination of information,  delivery of services including online enrollment of farmers, uploading/obtaining individual insured famer’s details and transfer of claim amount electronically to the individual farmer’s Bank Account. 
  • In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module namely ‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims from Kharif 2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) with Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and accounting system of Insurance Companies to provide timely & transparent processing of all claims.
  • W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance Company, penalty.of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP.  
  • Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate claims relating to the Central Government share.
  • 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in release of State share of subsidy.
  • Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for deposit of their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme has been made mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial discipline. 
  • Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data through CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance companies to witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records with NCIP and usage of remote sensing based yield estimation through YES-TECH have already been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to farmers.
  • Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application to streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for loacalised calamities/post harvest losses for individual farms and  land parcels under PMFBY.  The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the States/UTs under the scheme.

This information was given by the Union Minister of state for Agriculture and Farmers welfare, SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PROGRESS OF NATURAL FARMING UNDER THE NATIONAL MISSION FOR NATURAL FARMING
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet approved the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) on 25th November 2024 as a centrally sponsored scheme which is being implemented across the country to promote natural farming. Natural Farming is a chemical free farming, involving livestock integrated natural farming methods and diversified crop systems rooted in the Indian traditional knowledge. Natural farming improves soil health, restores ecosystems and reduces input cost to the farmer to achieve greater climate resilience. Natural farming recognises the interdependence of the natural ecosystem amongst soil, water, microbiome, plants, animals, climate and human requirements. State/UT wise details of the number of farmers covered, area brought under natural farming, and the clusters formed under the Mission (2024-25 and 2025-26) is given at Annexure - I.

Under the Mission, 527 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), 76 Agriculture Universities (AUs), 194 Local Natural farming Institutes (LNFIs) have been identified to support cluster level implementation of the scheme. 18 Centres of Natural Farming Institutes (CoNFs) have been identified that provide training of Scientists (from these (KVKs)/(SAUs), Officials of State/Districts/Block level implementing the scheme and Farmer Master Trainers (FMTs).  At a cluster level Community Resource Persons (CRPs) are deployed to handhold the farmers on the practices of Natural Farming.  So far, 33,257 Krishi Sakhis/Community Resource Persons (CRPs) have been trained at Krishi Vigyan Kendras(KVKs)/Agricultural Universities (AUs)/Local Natural Farming Institutions (LNFIs) under the Mission.

item.dc:creator: National Human Rights Commission
item.description: National Human Rights Commission NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual harassment of girl students by the Principal of a government school in Moga district, Punjab Issues notices to the state Chief Secretary and Moga SSP, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that the Principal of a government school in Moga district, Punjab sexually harassed several girl students by inappropriately…
item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual harassment of girl students by the Principal of a government school in Moga district, Punjab
Issues notices to the state Chief Secretary and Moga SSP, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that the Principal of a government school in Moga district, Punjab sexually harassed several girl students by inappropriately touching them. Reportedly, he used to threaten the students that he would fail them in the examination, if they complained against him in this regard.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violation. Therefore, it has issued notices to the state Chief Secretary and Moga Senior Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 23rd July 2026, the incident came to light when one of the victims informed her parents. The parents of the aggrieved girl called the Village Panchayat and reached the school to confront the Principal, who denied the allegation. However, several other girl students came forward making similar charges against him. The Police was also called.

*****

NSK

item.title: CLIMATE RISK AND CROP INSURANCE
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare CLIMATE RISK AND CROP INSURANCE Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) is mainly implemented on ‘Area Approach’ basis wherein claims are worked out on the area of the land parcel based on the shortfall in actual yield of the crop insured, submitted by the State Government concerned, on the basis of Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) as well as technology based yield estimated under YES-TECH (wherever applicable),…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
CLIMATE RISK AND CROP INSURANCE
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) is mainly implemented on ‘Area Approach’ basis wherein claims are worked out on the area of the land parcel based on the shortfall in actual yield of the crop insured, submitted by the State Government concerned, on the basis of Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) as well as technology based yield estimated under YES-TECH (wherever applicable), vis-à-vis threshold yield, as per the formula in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme.

However, losses due to localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloud burst & natural fire and post-harvest losses due to cyclone, cyclonic/unseasonal rains & hailstorms are calculated on individual insured farm basis under PMFBY and RWBCIS. The extent of loss and claims in such case are assessed by a joint committee comprising representatives of State Government and concerned insurance company within stipulated timeframe under the Operational Guidelines of the scheme.

Further, as per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT).

At the field level, loss assessment under SDRF is done through a joint field survey by Revenue and Agriculture Department officials. Input subsidy becomes payable only where crop loss is assessed at 33% or more. For SDRF, the State conducts its own assessment whereas for NDRF assistance, the State submits a memorandum to the Government of India, after which an IMCT visits and physically verifies the damage.

The loss assessment under SDRF and NDRF is done only during natural calamities in the specific area of the State and is not a regular District level crop loss assessment. Hence, the same cannot be compared with claims settled under PMFBY and RWBCIS. 

Following steps have been taken by Govt. of India to for timely settlement of claims under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana:

  • Government has undertaken development of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) as a single source of data for subsidy payment, dissemination of information,  delivery of services including online enrollment of farmers, uploading/obtaining individual insured famer’s details and transfer of claim amount electronically to the individual farmer’s Bank Account. 
  • In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module namely ‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims from Kharif 2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) with Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and accounting system of Insurance Companies to provide timely & transparent processing of all claims.
  • W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance Company, penalty.of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP.  
  • Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate claims relating to the Central Government share.
  • 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in release of State share of subsidy.
  • Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for deposit of their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme has been made mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial discipline. 
  • Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data through CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance companies to witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records with NCIP and usage of remote sensing-based yield estimation through YES-TECH have already been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to farmers.
  • Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application to streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for loacalised calamities/post-harvest losses for individual farms and land parcels under PMFBY.  The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the States/UTs under the scheme.

This information was given by the Union Minister of state for Agriculture and Farmers welfare, SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PROGRESS IN GENERATING UNIQUE DIGITAL FARMER IDS
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

As of 20th July, 2026, more than 10.18 Crore Farmer IDs have been created to streamline the direct transfer of subsidies and technical advisories. The State-wise progress of Farmer IDs generated is placed at Annexure-I. States are using Farmer IDs to ease the lives of farmers. It enables the integration of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) schemes such as registrations under Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojna (PM Kisan), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY), Minimum Support Price (MSP) based procurement, access to credit delivery, input distribution, and disaster relief.

The integration of satellite imagery has optimized and streamlined the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) operations through the following initiatives:

  1. Yield Estimation System based on Technology (YES-TECH): Satellite Remote sensing data, coupled with various crop yield estimation models, is leveraged to generate technology based crop yield at Insurance unit level. This significantly supplements Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) yield data, addressing localized yield anomalies with high accuracy.
  2. Smart Sampling for Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs): Instead of random field selections, satellite- derived vegetation indices identify variations in crop health and this allows optimization of the planning of CCEs, eliminating manual selection biases and accelerating data collection.
  3. Dispute Resolution: Remote sensing provides an objective assessment of crop conditions across seasons using time series satellite images. This data serves as an effective tool to resolve area discrepancy and yield disputes between State Governments and Insurance Companies in short turn-around time, eliminating delays in claim settlements.
  4. Rapid Crop Damage & Inundation Assessment: In the event of localized natural calamities like floods, droughts, or severe weather anomalies, multi-temporal satellite imagery enables rapid mapping of the affected area. Through the automated workflows of the Krishi Decision Support System (DSS), the turnaround time for assessment of food inundation and drought monitoring has significantly reduced.

The various initiatives have been taken to train and equip for utilizing agricultural drones, such as use of drones are promoted under Sub-Mission on Agriculture Mechanization (SMAM) by providing assistance up to 50% for agriculture graduates, Small and Marginal farmers of the North Eastern States for procuring kisan drones. For other farmers, financial assistance for the purchase of Kisan Drones is provided at 40% of the cost. Financial assistance of 40% of the cost is also provided for establishing Custom Hiring Centres of Kisan Drones. A total of 2122 Drones have been distributed/approved under SMAM scheme.

The Farm Machinery Training & Testing Institutes (FMTTIs), which are subordinate offices of the Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare located at Budni (Madhya Pradesh), Hisar (Haryana), and Biswanath Chariali (Assam), are DGCA-approved RPTOs conducting training on drones. To date, these institutes have trained 155 drone pilots. The expenditure towards these training programmes is met by the Institutes from their annual budget.

The comprehensive 15-day training programme on the operation of agricultural drones, including obtaining a Drone Pilot Licence, is an integral component of the drone supply package under the Namo Drone Didi Scheme. As the scheme is exclusively for the identified Women Self Help Groups (SHGs), the members of each selected SHG are trained as drone pilots. These trainings are conducted in Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) approved Remote Pilot Training Organization (RPTOs), which are presently 274 in number across the country. Under this scheme, 1094 drones have been provided to the selected SHGs.

item.content:encoded:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
Two-day Orientation Programme for Newly Elected and Nominated Members of Rajya Sabha begins tomorrow
Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan to inaugurate the Orientation Programme
Senior Rajya Sabha Members and Officers of the Secretariat to guide newly elected and nominated Members
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

Experienced sitting Members of Rajya Sabha and senior officers of the Secretariat will guide the newly elected and nominated Members on the topics related to the procedures and functioning of Parliament, particularly Rajya Sabha, during a two-day Orientation Programme to be inaugurated tomorrow by Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan.

The Rajya Sabha Secretariat is organising a two-day interactive programme on 25th and 26th July, 2026 for the benefit of newly elected and nominated Members of Rajya Sabha. The two-day Orientation Programme will begin with a Welcome Address by Hon'ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh.

Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan will deliver ‘Keynote address outlining the vision and responsibilities of the Members’; Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Shri Harivansh will speak on ‘The functions and roles of key Parliamentary Committees’; Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, M/o Railways; Information & Broadcasting; and Electronics & Information Technology will speak on ‘Hands-on IT workshop: Understanding the impact of AI, Blockchain, and Data Privacy laws on future legislation and public service delivery’ during the two-day programme. Other senior Members of Parliament viz. Dr. John Brittas, Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari, Shri Sujeet Kumar and Shri Pramod Tiwari are also likely to conduct interactive sessions of legislative relevance during the programme.

Shri P.C. Mody, Secretary-General, Rajya Sabha will speak on ‘Introduction to the structure, functions, and services provided by the Secretariat and ‘Formal expression of gratitude to the dignitaries and attendees’. Other senior officers of Rajya Sabha Secretariat will speak on the topics of Parliamentary importance during the two-day programme. Dr. K.S. Somashekhar, Secretary will give the final Vote of Thanks marking the end of the two-day programme.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
PROGRESS UNDER DDU-GKY
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

DDU-GKY is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement linked skilling programs.

Under DDU-GKY, efforts are made to align the aspirations of rural youth with the evolving skill requirements of the labour market. States/UTs are provided budgetary support to undertake skill gap studies to identify sectoral opportunities and employment potential in their regions. Based on these studies, States/UTs and Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are encouraged to propose training programmes in emerging and high-growth sectors aligned with local, domestic and global job markets. While submitting project proposals, PIAs are required to provide justification and demand assessment for the sectors proposed, ensuring that training under DDU-GKY remains demand-driven and industry-relevant.

So far under DDUGKY, a total of 18.45 lakh candidates has been trained and 12.35 lakh have been placed till June 2026.

The sectors that have been identified for the training and placement of rural youth under the said scheme are given as Annexure I.

Funds are released to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), subject to achieving the placement target. PIAs are required to ensure placement of at least 70% of trained candidates, with at least 50% placed in wage employment. Post Placement Support (PPS) is provided to eligible candidates to facilitate retention for a period of six months and tracking for up to twelve months.

The Budget Estimate (BE) for the FY 2026-27 is ₹ 750.00 crore as Central Share.

This information was given by Minister of State for the Rural Development, Shri Kamlesh Paswan in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
STATUS OF IMPLEMENTATION OF PMGSY
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Under the various ongoing verticals of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), a total of 2,905 roads covering 15,647.78 km and 1,042 bridges were completed across the country during the financial year 2025–26. In addition, 93 eligible habitations were provided with all-weather road connectivity.

Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana-I (PMGSY-I) was launched as a one-time special intervention to provide rural connectivity, by way of a single all-weather road, to the eligible unconnected habitations in the core network for uplifting the socio-economic condition of the rural population. Under this scheme 1,62,876 habitations were provided connectivity. This scheme was closed on 31.03.2025 and no new further sanction was issued. However, timeline extension was given up to 31.03.2027 to complete any of the balance works and payments. Subsequently, new intervention/verticals namely PMGSY-II for up-gradation of 50,000 Km of the existing rural roads and PMGSY-III for consolidation of 1, 25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations, inter-alia, to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals, were added under the ambit of PMGSY. PMGSY II and III are schemes to provide all weather connectivity to habitations and connectivity to government institutions. Since September 2024, PMGSY-IV has been launched with an objective to provide connectivity to 25000 unconnected habitations by the year 2029.

State/UT wise details may be accessed at home page of programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in >habitations coverage.

(b) & (c): The implementation plan for PMGSY during the Financial Year 2026–27 focuses on the timely completion of ongoing works and up-gradation of rural roads and strengthening the maintenance of the already constructed roads. The key components of the implementation plan are as follows:

(i)  Expeditious completion of ongoing works sanctioned under the various verticals of PMGSY (except PMGSY II which has been closed since 31.03.2026).

(ii)  Sanction of rural roads projects under PMGSY-IV, in accordance with the approved framework and scheme guidelines, to provide all weather connectivity to unconnected habitations.

(iii)  Maintenance of PMGSY roads by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations in accordance with the programme guidelines.

(iv)  Strengthening digital maintenance management through the Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads (eMARG) platform for planning, inspections, performance-based payments and monitoring of maintenance works.

(v)  Quality assurance through the three-tier quality monitoring mechanism comprising Programme Implementation Units (PIUs), State Quality Monitors (SQMs) and National Quality Monitors (NQMs), and supplemented by geo-tagged inspections.

(vi)  Regular monitoring and capacity building through review meetings, Regional Review Meetings (RRMs), field inspections and advisories to ensure timely implementation, quality construction and sustainable maintenance of rural road assets.

These measures are aimed at achieving the annual physical targets for FY 2026–27 while ensuring durable, high-quality rural road infrastructure and improved connectivity across the country. Accordingly, a target has been fixed for the completion of 26,474 km of rural roads, 1,375 bridges and connectivity to 2,400 eligible habitations, during FY 2026–27, under the various verticals of PMGSY, including PMGSY-I, PMGSY-III, Road Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas (RCPLWEA), PM-JANMAN and PMGSY-IV (given at Annexure-I).

Under PMGSY, special emphasis is accorded to improving rural road connectivity in Aspirational Districts, tribal areas, Left Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas and other remote and difficult regions, in accordance with the scheme guidelines and approved framework. Accordingly, the Government has adopted the following mechanisms to prioritize road connectivity in such areas:

(i)  Priority to eligible unconnected habitations located in Aspirational Districts, tribal and remote areas while preparing proposals under the relevant verticals of PMGSY, subject to eligibility under the scheme by identifying such projects under Comprehensive New Connectivity Priority List (CNCPL). The sanctions and implementation of projects are done as per the CNCPL list.

(ii)  Dedicated interventions such as the Road Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas (RCPLWEA) to improve connectivity in LWE-affected districts.

(iii)  Population norms relaxation are also provided in these areas 250+ in North-Eastern States, Hill States/UTs & special category areas and 100+ in LWE affected districts, which have become eligible as per 2011 census.

(iv)  PM-JANMAN, under which road connectivity is being provided to eligible Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) habitations with a population of 100+, to improve access to essential services and socio-economic opportunities.

These measures are intended to promote balanced regional development and improve access to education, healthcare, markets and other essential services in underserved rural areas.

The fund-sharing pattern of PMGSY is in the ratio of 60:40 between the Centre and States for all States and UTs with Legislature except 8 North-East (NE) States and 2 Himalayan States and 1 UT (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir). It is 90:10 between the Centre and States for 8 NE States including Sikkim and 2 Himalayan States and 1 UT (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir) and 100% central share for UTs without legislature (Andaman & Nicobar and Ladakh). The funds are released on the basis of works in hand, the progress achieved in the project and after due submission of necessary documents. The fund releases under PMGSY is through the SNA SPARSH system. The details of budget allocation and sanction for the FY 2026-27 is given in Annexure-II.

This information was given by Minister of State for the Rural Development, Shri Kamlesh Paswan in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMAY-G
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G) is reviewed through Performance Review Committee (PRC) Meetings, Empowered Committee (EC) Meetings, Common Review Mission (CRM), Area Officers Schemes, Reports of National Level Monitors etc. besides regular field visits by the officers of the Ministry. Recently, the Empowered Committee (EC) Meetings have been held in the month of March 2026. Further, the State-wise details of houses sanctioned, completed and pending as of June, 2026 are provided in Annexure – I.

The Government has approved the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) with the unit assistance of Rs. 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs. 1.30 lakh in North Eastern States, Hilly States (including UTs of J&K and Ladakh). In addition to the unit assistance provided under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹12,000 is extended for the construction of toilets through convergence with the Swachh Bharat Mission–Gramin (SBM-G). Further, there is a provision for providing prescribed person-days of unskilled wage employment within the approved scheme parameters, at prevailing wage rates to each PMAY-G beneficiary for the construction of their house through convergence with MGNREGS/ VB G-RAM G.

This information was given by Minister of State for the Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
SHGS FORMED UNDER DAY-NRLM
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

Under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) have been formed across the country, covering 10.05 crore rural women.

Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry is promoting financial inclusion of women Self Help Group (SHG) members through financial literacy, enhanced access to institutional credit, and promotion of micro-enterprises.

To deepen financial inclusion in rural areas, particularly among women SHG members, DAY-NRLM has launched a comprehensive Financial Literacy Programme in partnership with Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) and banks. Financial Literacy Community Resource Persons conduct village-level financial literacy camps covering modules on Financial Planning, Savings, Credit, Insurance, Pension, Enterprise Financing, and Business Correspondence. During the Financial Year 2025–26, more than 3.81 crore women SHG members were imparted financial literacy training on these modules.

Further, all Public Sector Banks and one private sector bank have designed their own dedicated credit products for individual women SHG members under DAY-NRLM to facilitate the Lakhpati Didi initiative. These credit products enable women SHG members to establish new enterprises or expand their existing enterprises by availing institutional credit at affordable rates.

During the Financial Year 2025–26, the total turnover from the marketing of products manufactured by women Self Help Groups under DAY-NRLM through Saras Aajeevika Stores and e-commerce platforms is as under:-

item.title: EMPLOYMENT GENERATION UNDER VB-G RAM G SCHEME
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Rural Development

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
EMPLOYMENT GENERATION UNDER VB-G RAM G SCHEME
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Government continuously reviews the implementation of the programme in consultation with the States/UTs and takes appropriate measures to address implementation-related issues. Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, employment was provided to all rural households that demanded work, in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The number of person-days generated varied across States/UTs and financial years depending upon the demand for employment registered by rural households.

The year-wise and States/Union Territories-wise details of persondays generated under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS during the last five financial years is given at Annexure.

For Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, which has been operationalized with effect from 01.07.2026 a comprehensive online Management Information System (MIS) has been put in place for real time monitoring of implementation and addressing the issues if any faced by implementing agencies. Further, Ministry has deputed large number of officers to the States to review its implementation and provide handholding support to States.

To ensure timely wage payments, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), under which wages are directly credited into the bank accounts of beneficiaries. The Ministry has also issued detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) prescribing timelines and responsibilities at various levels for timely processing of wage payments. Further, technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) are used for real-time monitoring and tracking of wage payments, pendency at different stages, and regular review with the States/UTs to facilitate timely resolution of issues. In addition, the Ministry regularly releases funds to the States/UTs based on the actual demand from ground and fulfilment of statutory and financial requirements, to ensure smooth implementation of the programme.

The Government has enacted the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, which has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 across all rural areas of the country. The Act strengthens the rural employment guarantee framework by enhancing the statutory employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days per rural household in a financial year.

The Government has made adequate budgetary provision for effective implementation of the programme. For the financial year 2026–27, a Central share of ₹95,692.31 crore has been provided for the Scheme, representing the highest-ever Budget Estimate for rural employment. With the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is expected to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore.

To ensure timely wage disbursal, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and established technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) for real-time monitoring and review of wage payments.

The Act accords high priority to Livelihood-related Infrastructure as one of its core thematic areas and adopts a Whole-of-Government Approach through convergence with agriculture, allied sectors and other Government programmes. It permits the creation of rural infrastructure such as Skill Development Centres, Rural Libraries, Digital Learning Centres and other community assets that promote skilling, learning and sustainable livelihoods.

This information was given by Minister of State for the Rural Development, Shri Kamlesh Paswan in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

*The release of funds to the State of West Bengal under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS was stopped with effect from 09.03.2022 by invoking the provisions of Section 27 of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, owing to continued non-compliance with the directives of the Central Government by the State. Hence, no fund was released to State during the last five financial years.

As per the request made by and following clarifications provided by the State Government, implementation of Scheme has been resumed in the State w.e.f. 01.06.2026, and accordingly, Labour Budget for the month of June 2026 was approved. Further, on implementation of VB- G RAM G in the State from 01.07.2026 necessary normative allocation has been made and Mother sanction for release of fund has also been issued.

India Successfully Hosts 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction; BRICS Joint Statement Adopted to Advance Global Disaster Resilience
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

Under India's BRICS Chairship 2026, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, successfully hosted the BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) in New Delhi on 24 July 2026. The Meeting was chaired by Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Nityanand Rai, and attended by Ministers and Heads of Delegation from BRICS Member Countries, reaffirming their shared commitment to strengthening disaster resilience through enhanced cooperation, innovation and sustainable development.

The Meeting marked a significant milestone in the evolution of BRICS cooperation on disaster risk reduction and concluded with the unanimous adoption of the BRICS Joint Statement on Disaster Risk Reduction, reaffirming the collective commitment of Member Countries to accelerate implementation of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Work Plan (2025–2028) and deepen cooperation for building resilient societies.

Addressing the Ministerial Meeting, Shri Nityanand Rai stated that the evolution of BRICS cooperation—from the Udaipur Declaration (2016) to the Kazan Declaration (2024) and the establishment of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Group (DRRG)—reflects the growing recognition that disaster risk reduction is central to sustainable development, climate resilience and human security. He noted that under India's BRICS Chairship, the Group has adopted a practical and action-oriented approach under the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," and appreciated Brazil for elevating the DRR Group to the Ministerial level.

Highlighting India's leadership in disaster risk reduction, the Minister said that India's people-centric approach is guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Ten-Point Agenda for Disaster Risk Reduction. He emphasized India's five strategic priorities under its Chairship to accelerate implementation of the BRICS DRR Work Plan (2025–2028) and called upon Member Countries to strengthen cooperation in science and technology, early warning systems, resilient infrastructure, nature-based solutions and community resilience to make disaster risk reduction an integral part of sustainable development.

The Ministerial Meeting featured a High-Level Policy Dialogue on "Advancing Climate-Smart and Disaster-Resilient Infrastructure Systems: Partnerships, Innovation and Financing for Resilient Development," where Ministers deliberated on resilient infrastructure, innovative financing, emerging technologies and international partnerships to address increasing disaster and climate risks.

A Ministerial Roundtable on "Accelerating Implementation of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Work Plan (2025–2028)" enabled Member Countries to exchange experiences and identify practical pathways for strengthening institutional cooperation, capacity building, knowledge sharing and implementation of the agreed priorities.

As part of India's Chairship, six flagship knowledge products were launched to support evidence-based policymaking, institutional strengthening, capacity building and practical implementation of disaster risk reduction initiatives across BRICS Member Countries.

As a way forward, the Ministers emphasized strengthening practical and action-oriented cooperation through regular technical exchanges, joint projects, simulation exercises, technical expert exchanges and annual thematic workstreams to promote knowledge sharing, innovation and measurable outcomes in disaster resilience.

The successful conclusion of the 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction reinforces BRICS' collective commitment to advancing resilient, inclusive and sustainable development through strengthened international cooperation on disaster risk reduction.

item.description: Ministry of Power Meeting of Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Power Held Committee discusses consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi The Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Power met yesterday under the chairmanship of Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, to deliberate on the proposed framework for parallel distribution licensing aimed at promoting consumer choice, improving service quality and ensuring efficient utilisation of electricity distribution…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Power
Meeting of Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Power Held
Committee discusses consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Power met yesterday under the chairmanship of Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, to deliberate on the proposed framework for parallel distribution licensing aimed at promoting consumer choice, improving service quality and ensuring efficient utilisation of electricity distribution infrastructure. The meeting was attended by Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power, Members of Parliament who are members of the Consultative Committee, Secretary, Ministry of Power and senior officials of Ministry of Power.

Addressing the Committee, the Union Minister stated that the Electricity Act, 2003 had successfully introduced competition in electricity generation, transmission and trading, while distribution remains the only major segment where competition continues to be limited. He emphasised that as India moves towards becoming a developed nation under the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, consumers will increasingly expect reliable, affordable and high-quality electricity supply comparable to global standards.

It was discussed that while the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, it requires each licensee to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of poles, lines and substations, increases capital expenditure and discourages fresh investment, ultimately leading to inefficient utilisation of resources.

The proposed framework seeking to enable competition in electricity supply without requiring duplication of the physical distribution network was discussed in detail. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks. New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned State Electricity Regulatory Commission.

The Minister highlighted that the detailed implementation framework would be developed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to ensure fairness, transparency and non-discriminatory access to the network. The proposal also fully protects the interests of incumbent distribution licensees and their employees. Further, all distribution licensees will continue to be bound by the universal service obligation under the Electricity Act, and the regulatory framework will prevent selective supply only to profitable consumers.

Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Shri Manohar Lal stated that consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecommunications and aviation. Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure.

The Minister noted that the concept is not new to India and has been successfully implemented in Mumbai for several years, where consumers have exercised supplier choice while the distribution network continues to be developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the State Electricity Regulatory Commission.

The members of Parliament participated actively in the discussions and offered valuable suggestions on various aspects of the proposed framework. Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power thanked the Members for their constructive inputs and reaffirmed the Government's commitment to carrying forward reforms that place consumers at the centre of India's power sector while ensuring efficiency, transparency and sustainable growth.

Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
SAGARMALA PROGRAMME AND PORT MODERNISATION
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

Sagarmala scheme is a central sector scheme of Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) with the target to promote port-led development in the country. Under this scheme, MoPSW provides financial assistance for the projects under 5 pillars namely, port modernization, port connectivity, port-led industrialization, coastal community development, and coastal shipping & inland water transport. The pillar wise progress of the projects funded under Sagarmala scheme is available at Annexure-I.
                                                                                                                        Annexure I

Government has taken several measures to enhance port capacity, improve operational efficiency, and reduce vessel turnaround time at major ports. Infrastructure development and capacity augmentation is a continuous process and includes construction of new berths and terminals, mechanization, modernization and optimization of existing berths and terminals, capital dredging to deepen drafts for accommodating larger vessels, development of road and rail connectivity, and creation of supporting infrastructure such as parking plazas. Further, port processes have been streamlined with the implementation of One Nation One Port Process (ONOP) to improve operational efficiency and reduce vessel turnaround time. As a result of these initiatives, the cargo handling capacity of the Major and Other than Major Ports (OTMP) has increased to 2,818 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) as on March 2026 from ~1,400 MTPA in 2013-14.


One of the objectives of Sagarmala programme is better port connectivity, efficient cargo movement between ports and their respective hinterland to minimize overall logistics cost. Sagarmala programme has a dedicated pillar of port connectivity which focuses on the last mile and immediate hinterland connectivity of the ports via road, rail and inland waterways. Further, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has undertaken a comprehensive assessment of port connectivity and prepared a Comprehensive Port Connectivity Plan (CPCP) in 2022 by reviewing connectivity of the operational ports and identified the ports which needed improvement of road and/ or rail connectivity with nearby economic hubs.

Subsequently, MoPSW in consultation with Ministry of Road, Transport and Highways and Ministry of Railways has identified a total of 294 rail and road connectivity projects, out of which, 84 projects (63 Rail and 21 Road) have been completed, 66 projects (27 Rail and 39 Road) are under implementation, and a total of 144 projects (42 Rail and 102 Road) are under planning stage. The connectivity projects within the port limits are taken up by the Port Authorities and beyond the port limits are taken up by Ministries like MoR, MoRTH or State Governments.

As regard to inland waterway connectivity projects, details of projects completed by Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) on National Waterways (NW) are as under:

3 Multi Modal Terminals (MMTs) and 01 intermodal terminal on NW 1

1 MMT and 3 IWT terminals on NW 2

9 IWT terminals on NW 3;

02 Roll-on/Roll-off (Ro-Ro) terminals in Ernakulam

01 Ro-Ro terminal on NW 4

The MoPSW has sanctioned financial assistance of ₹ 272 crore to 9 projects worth

₹ 1,286 crore under Sagarmala scheme in the state of Andhra Pradesh and the details of these projects are available at Annexure-II. These projects are related to Ro-Pax and passenger jetties, fishing harbours, port modernization and skill development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
REVAMPING OF SHIPBUILDING INDUSTRY
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has reviewed India's Shipbuilding sector following the  announcement of measures under the Union Budget 2025–26 and adopted a 4-pillar  strategy to revitalize the shipbuilding sector. The Government has accordingly approved a  comprehensive package of ₹ 69,725 crore to strengthen domestic shipbuilding  capacity, maritime financing and skilling. The key components of the shipbuilding  package include: 
 

Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), an extension of  Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to  address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards; 

Maritime Development Fund (MDF) corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore for providing long  term financing support to shipbuilding and maritime sector comprising a Maritime  Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore and Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) of ₹  5,000 crore; 
 

Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS) with ₹19,989 crore outlay to expand  Indian shipbuilding output capacity to 4.5 million Gross Tonnage annually by setting up greenfield shipbuilding clusters and capacity expansion of the existing  shipyards. These targets have been set to position India as a competitive global  shipbuilding force in line with the vision contained in Maritime India Vision 2030 and  Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 documents.
 

Policy reforms have been undertaken to revamp the shipbuilding industry including  implementation of classification of large vessels as infrastructure and demand  aggregation. The government on 19th September 2025, notified infrastructure status to  Indian-flagged commercial vessels with a Gross Tonnage (GT) of 10,000 or above. For  vessels constructed in India infrastructure status was accorded to vessels of size 1,500  GT or above. As part of demand aggregation, a fleet acquisition plan of 400+ vessels  has been prepared which provides long term order visibility to the Indian shipyards. 

The scheme guidelines to operationalize SBFAS have been issued on  26.12.2025 and in-principle approvals for shipbuilding financial support are given in  accordance with scheme guidelines. The guidelines for MDF have also been issued  on 20.02.2026. Further, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed as the Fund  Manager for MIF on 26.05.2026. 

As on-date, under SbDS, Government has accorded in-principle approval for  the development of three greenfield shipbuilding clusters at Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat  and Tamil Nadu. SbDS provides financial assistance for development of common  maritime and land based infrastructure for the greenfield clusters. Further, under SbDS,  the India Ship Technology Centre (ISTC) has been established as a Section 8 company  to promote the overall development of the Indian shipbuilding sector by enhancing  capabilities in ship design, research and development (R&D), skill development,  software, and other related areas. As regards skilling development, the details of  various steps taken are as under: 

11 shipyards have signed MoUs with 34 ITIs across 8 coastal States towards  implementation of on the job training (OJTs). As part of this, a 150-hour OJT model has  been introduced. 727 trainees have already been trained till date in these yards. 

Training of Trainers (ToT) program has been implemented at 2 Industrial  Training Institutes (ITIs) in West Bengal by Centre of Excellence in Maritime and  Shipbuilding (CEMS). 


A preliminary Skill Gap Study has been completed across 9 shipyards.

A total of 92,697 candidates have been trained/skilled/upskilled during the last  3 years.
 

A Plan of Implementation (PoI) has been signed between MoPSW and Korea  International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) for a skill development project in the  shipbuilding sector. 

As per the latest UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) report, India’s  shipbuilding output increased by 41% from 40,923 GT in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025 .  The comprehensive shipbuilding package of Government of India has instilled  confidence in Indian shipyards, resulting in the placement of several large commercial  and export shipbuilding orders to existing shipyards. In the last two years in-principle  approvals have been given for financial assistance under SBFAP and SPFAS to the Indian  shipyards for a total contract value of ₹15,234 crore. Under the SbDS scheme, so far,  in-principle approval has been given to proposals of four shipyards for brownfield  capacity augmentation of their facilities for ship-building and ship-repair at a total  estimated cost of over ₹2,500 crore. Given the high employment multiplier of 6.4 in the shipbuilding industry, the above developments have catalysed generation of large  numbers of direct as well as indirect employment. 

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN MARITIME SECTOR
Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

To strengthen employment opportunities in the maritime sector, the Government has undertaken a multi-pronged strategy for capacity building. Since completion of onboard sea-time training is an essential requirement for certification and career progression, initiatives have been taken to augment training capacity, strengthen industry participation and create additional onboard training opportunities, thereby enhancing the employability of Indian maritime trainees and supporting the long-term growth of the maritime workforce. As part of these initiatives, 96 training berths have been created on the passenger vessel MV Swaraj Dweep of the Andaman & Nicobar Administration in collaboration with the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), benefiting General Purpose (GP) Rating and Certificate Course in Maritime Catering (CCMC) candidates.

To promote cargo transportation and economic activities through the development of inland waterways, Government declared 111 (5 pre-existing and 106 new) National Waterways (NWs) in the country vide National Waterways Act, 2016. Action plans for development for NWs have been drawn under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 by the Government. Initiatives as Infrastructure and Policy measures taken to promote cargo transportation through the inland water transportation are detailed at Annexure-1. Due to these measures, the cargo movement on National Waterways increased from 18 million tons in 2013-14 to 218 million tons in 2025-26. Details of cargo transportation through inland waterways year-wise, from 2014 to 2026 and active seafarers are placed at Annexure-2.

Annexure-1

Infrastructure and Policy measures taken by the Government for promotion and modernize Inland Water Transport on NWs:

 Infrastructure measures: 

 Fairway maintenance works (river training, maintenance dredging, channel marking and regular hydrographic surveys) are taken up in various National Waterways (NWs) for providing a navigation channel of 35/45 m width and 2.0 / 2.2 / 2.5 / 3.0 m least available depth (LAD) for operation of vessels.

 66 community jetties, 20 floating terminals, 3 Multi-Modal Terminals (MMTs), 1 Inter-Modal Terminal (IMT) and 4 Ro-Pax terminals have been constructed on NW-1 (River Ganga) in addition to 5 pre-existing permanent terminals.

13 floating terminals provided on NW-2 (River Brahmaputra) along with MMTs at Pandu, Jogighopa and terminals at Bogibeel and Dhubri. Four dedicated Jetties for cruise vessels have been provided at Jogighopa, Pandu, Biswanath Ghat and Neamati. In addition to this, Jetties for cruise and passengers have been constructed at Sadiya, Lyka and Orium Ghat in Assam.

2 existing terminals at Badarpur & Karimganj on NW-16 (the Barak) have been upgraded/renovated and the terminal at Sonamura on river Gumati in Tripura under IBP route has been constructed.

 9 Permanent Inland Water Transport terminals with godowns and 2 Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax terminals have been constructed on NW-3 (West Coast Canal in Kerala).

 4 floating concrete jetties were provided to the Govt. of Goa and installed in Mandovi River (NW-68).

04 Tourist Jetties on NW-4 (River Krishna) in Andhra Pradesh have been commissioned and 8 Nos. floating jetties on NW-110 (River Yamuna) in Mathura-Vrindavan stretch in Uttar Pradesh, 2 Jetties on NW-73 (River Narmada) & 2 Jetties on NW-37 (River Gandak) in Bihar are established.

A new Navigation Lock at Farakka and 2 Nos. Quick Pontoon Opening Mechanisms (QPOMs) have been constructed on NW-1 to facilitate smooth & faster movement of vessels.

Policy Measures:

 A scheme for providing 35% incentive to promote the utilization of inland waterways transport sector by cargo owners and for scheduled service for cargo movement on NW-1 and NW-2 and NW-16 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government. This scheme is expected to divert 800 million tonne Km cargo on IWT mode, which is nearly 17% of the current cargo of 4700 million tonne Km on NWs. The scheme is implemented at a cost of INR 95.42 Crore for three years and can be scaled up or modified depending on the success of the scheme.

An extension of the tonnage tax scheme to inland vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 is announced during the budget presented on 01.02.2025. Inland vessels operating on National Waterways, rivers, and canals, will be benefited. This move is expected to boost the industry's competitiveness and encourage more cargo owners to use inland waterways for transportation. A tonnage tax system is a special taxation policy for shipping companies where tax is not based on actual profits but on the size (tonnage) of the vessel. It provides stable, predictable, and lower taxation for vessel owners, reducing their financial burden.

The National Waterways (Construction of Jetties / Terminals) Regulations 2025 has been notified, allowing private companies to invest and operate Inland Waterways infrastructure by providing a clear regulatory framework to attract private sector investment for facilitating the growth of inland waterways sector.

Jalyan & Navic : To increase ease of doing business in the IWT sector, along the same lines as ‘vahan’ and ‘sarathi’, a central data base and portal has been developed for registration of vessels and crew all over the country. This will facilitate registration of vessels and crew digitally and would also provide accurate status on the number of vessels and crew in the country and thus help in planning.

Cargo Aggregation : The cargo movement on the waterways suffer from problems of multimodality because of lack of industries along the waterways. Therefore, projects for development of cargo aggregation hub – MMLP at Varanasi and Integrated Cluster-cum-Logistics Park, Sahibganj have been taken up. NHLML, a PSU under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been engaged for development of these MMLPs. The work of Rail connectivity for three MMTs has been assigned to M/s Indian Port and Rail Company Ltd. (A PSU under MoPSW).

IBP Route : Indo Bangladesh Protocol route no. 5 & 6 between Maia and Sultanganj has been operationalized recently with successful trial movements. Regular movement shall commence shortly, once the consent of Bangladesh Side is received.

Shift of cargo by PSUs : For modal shift of cargo to waterways, more than 140 Public Sector Units have been approached to plan their movement using Inland Water Transport mode. They have been requested to outline their current status of cargo

movement through the waterways and their plan for modal shift of cargo. The Ministry of PNG, Co-operation/ Fertiliser, Food & Public distribution, Heavy industries, Steel and Coal have been requested to advise the PSUs under their jurisdiction to utilise IWT mode as far as possible and earmark certain percentage of their cargo for IWT mode keeping in line the MIV targets.
