The various safety measures taken to enhance safety in train operations are as under:-

1.        On Indian Railways, the expenditure on Safety related activities has increased over the years as under:-

Year

Expenditure/Budget on Safety related activities (Rs. in Cr.)

2013-14

1,20,389

 

2.     Electrical/Electronic Interlocking Systems with centralized operation of points and signals have been provided at 6,671 stations up to 30.06.2026 to reduce accidents due to human failure.

3.      Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates has been provided at 10,395 Level Crossing Gates up to 30.06.2026 for enhancing safety at LC Gates.

4.     Complete Track Circuiting of stations to enhance safety by verification of track occupancy by electrical means has been provided at 6,671 stations up to 30.06.2026.

5.     Detailed instructions on issues related with safety of Signalling, e.g. mandatory correspondence check, alteration work protocol, preparation of completion drawing, etc. have been issued.

6.           System of disconnection and reconnection for S&T equipment as per protocol has been re-emphasized.

7.           All locomotives are equipped with Vigilance Control Devices (VCD) to improve alertness of Loco Pilots.

8.        Retro-reflective sigma boards are provided on the mast which is located two OHE masts prior to the signals in electrified territories to alert the crew about the signal ahead when visibility is low due to foggy weather.

9.         A GPS based Fog Safety Device (FSD) is provided to loco pilots in fog affected areas which enables loco pilots to know the distance of the approaching landmarks like signals, level crossing gates, etc.

10.     Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) rails, Prestressed Concrete Sleeper (PSC) Normal/Wide base sleepers with elastic fastening, fan shaped layout turnout on PSC sleepers, Steel Channel/H-beam Sleepers on girder bridges is used while carrying out primary track renewals.

11.      Mechanisation of track laying activity through use of track machines like PQRS, TRT, T-28 etc. to reduce human errors.

12.     Maximizing supply of 130m/260m long rail panels for increasing progress of rail renewal and avoiding welding of joints, thereby improving safety.

13.        Ultrasonic Flaw Detection (USFD) testing of rails to detect flaws and timely removal of defective rails.

14.    Laying of longer rails, minimizing the use of Alumino Thermic Welding and adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e., Flash Butt Welding.

15.      Monitoring of track geometry by OMS (Oscillation Monitoring System) and TRC (Track Recording Cars).

16.       Patrolling of railway tracks to look out for weld/rail fractures.

17.      The use of Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossing in turnout renewal works.

18.      Inspections at regular intervals are carried out to monitor and educate staff for observance of safe practices.

19.     Web based online monitoring system of track assets viz. Track database and decision support system has been adopted to decide rationalized maintenance requirement and optimize inputs.

20.      Detailed instructions on issues related with safety of Track, e.g. integrated block, corridor block, worksite safety, monsoon precautions, etc. have been issued.

21.        Preventive maintenance of railway assets (Coaches & Wagons) is undertaken to ensure safe train operations.

22.       Replacement of conventional ICF design coaches with LHB design coaches is being done.

23.       All unmanned level crossings (UMLCs) on Broad Gauge (BG) route have been eliminated by January 2019.

24.     Safety of Railway Bridges is ensured through regular inspection of Bridges. The requirement of repair/rehabilitation of Bridges is taken up based upon the conditions assessed during these inspections.

25.     Indian Railways has displayed Statutory “Fire Notices” for widespread passenger information in all coaches. Fire posters are provided in every coach so as to educate and alert passengers regarding various Do’s and Don’ts to prevent fire. These include messages regarding not carrying any inflammable material, explosives, prohibition of smoking inside the coaches, penalties etc.

26.     Production Units are providing Fire detection and suppression system in newly manufactured Power Cars and Pantry Cars, Fire and Smoke detection system in newly manufactured coaches. Progressive fitment of the same in existing coaches is also underway by Zonal Railways in a phased manner.

27.       Regular counselling and training of staff is undertaken.

28.  Concept of Rolling Block introduced in Indian Railways (Open Lines) General Rules vide Gazette notification dated 30.11.2023, wherein work of integrated maintenance/ repair/replacement of assets is planned up to 52 weeks in advance on rolling basis and executed as per plan.

Implementation of Kavach:-

 

1.             Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system. Kavach is a highly technology intensive system, which requires safety certification of highest order (SIL-4).

2.             Kavach aids the Loco Pilot in running of trains within specified speed limits by automatic application of brakes in case Loco Pilot fails to do so and also helps the trains to run safely during inclement weather.

3.             The first field trials on the passenger trains were started in February 2016. Based on the experience gained and Independent Safety Assessment of the system by Independent Safety Assessor (ISA), three firms were approved in 2018-19, for supply of Kavach Ver 3.2.

4.             Kavach was adopted as National ATP system in July, 2020.

5.             Implementation of Kavach System involves following Key Activities:-

a.     Installation of Station Kavach at each and every station, block section.

b.     Installation of RFID Tags throughout the track length.

c.     Installation of telecom Towers throughout the section.

d.     Laying of Optical Fibre Cable along the track.

e.              Provision of Loco Kavach on each and every Locomotive running on Indian Railways.

6.             Based on deployment of Kavach version 3.2 on 1465 RKm on South Central Railway and experience gained, further improvements were made. Finally, Kavach specification version 4.0 was approved by RDSO on 16.07.2024.

7.             Kavach version 4.0 covers all the major features required for the diverse railway network. This is a significant milestone in safety for Indian Railways. Within a short period, IR has developed, tested and started deploying Automatic Train Protection System.

8.             Major improvement in Version 4.0 includes increased Location Accuracy, Improved Information of Signal Aspects in bigger yards, Station to Station Kavach interface on OFC and Direct Interface to existing Electronic Interlocking System. With these improvements, Kavach Ver.4.0. is planned for large scale deployment over Indian Railways.

9.             After extensive and elaborate trials, Kavach Version 4.0 has been successfully commissioned on 2490 Route Kilometres as on 13.07.2026, covering the high density Delhi- Mumbai and Delhi-Howrah routes as below:-

12.   In addition, work for installation of Kavach in 7,435 Locomotives and 1,200 EMU/MEMU has been taken up.

13.  Specialized training programmes on Kavach are being conducted at centralized training institutes of Indian Railways to impart training to all concerned officials. By now more than 94,000 technicians, operators and engineers have been trained on Kavach technology. This includes about 57,000 Loco Pilots & Assistant Loco Pilots. Courses have been designed in collaboration with IRISET.

14.  The funds utilized on Kavach works so far up to Jun’26 is Rs.3874.9 cr. The allocation of funds during the year 2026-27 is Rs.2066.24 crore. Requisite funds are made available as per the progress of works.

Inquiries into the rail accidents are carried out by the statutory bodies, the Commission of Railway Safety (CRS) under Ministry of Civil Aviation and the Departmental Inquiry Committees also as per laid down norms.

CRS of respective circles after due deliberations submit their findings and recommendations in accidents. Appropriate action is taken by the respective Railway administration on the recommendations, suggested by the CRS in their reports. The action taken reports address the deficiencies found and hence help avoiding recurrence of similar accidents.

This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Strengthens Workforce Through Mission-Mode Recruitment; Over 5.56 Lakh Recruitments Completed Since 2014 (Up to June 2026)
Recruitment Underway for Over 1.61 Lakh Vacancies Under the Annual Recruitment Calendar for 2024, 2025 and 2026
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi

Recruitment done in Indian Railways during 2004-05 to 2013-14 vis-à-vis during 2014-15 to 2025-26 is given as under: -

Period

Recruitments

2004-2005 to 2013-2014

4.11 lakh

2014-2015 to 2025-2026

5.53 lakh

2026-2027 (upto 30.06.2026)

3396

 

Occurrence and filling up of vacancies are continuous processes on Indian Railways considering its size, spatial distribution and criticality of operation. Adequate and suitable manpower is provided to cater to the regular operations, changes in technology, mechanisations and innovative practices. The vacancies are filled up primarily by placement of indents by Railways with Recruitment agencies as per operational and technological requirements.

The RRB examinations are quite technical in nature entailing large scale mobilization of men and resources and training of manpower. Railway overcame all these challenges and successfully conducted the recruitment in a transparent manner following all laid down guidelines. No instance of paper leakage or similar malpractice has occurred during the entire process.

Further, as system improvement, the Ministry of Railways has introduced a system of publishing the Annual Calendar from 2024 for recruitment to various categories of Group ‘C’ posts. The introduction of the Annual Calendar is benefitting the aspirants in the following manner:-

·                     More opportunities for candidates;

·                     Opportunities to those becoming eligible every year;

·                     Certainty of exams;

·                     Faster Recruitment process, Training and Appointments

Presently, recruitment against 1,61,889 vacancies of non-gazetted personnel has been taken up on Indian Railways as per Annual Calendar 2024, 2025 and 2026.

During January to December 2024, ten Centralized Employment Notifications (CENs) for 92,116 vacancies were notified for filling up of posts of Assistant Loco Pilots (ALPs), Technicians, Sub-Inspectors, Constables in Railway Protection Force (RPF), Junior Engineers (JEs)/ Depot Material Superintendent (DMS)/ Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA), Paramedical Categories, Non-Technical Popular Categories (Graduate), Non-Technical Popular Categories (Under-Graduate), Ministerial & Isolated Categories and Level-1 categories such as Assistants, Track Maintainers and Pointsman.

item.title: Government Strengthens Educational Opportunities for OBC, EBC and DNT Students through PM-YASASVI
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Educational Opportunities for OBC, EBC and DNT Students through PM-YASASVI PM-YASASVI Umbrella Scheme Provides Scholarship Support from Pre-Matric to Higher Education Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding educational opportunities for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC), Economically Backward Classes (EBC) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT) through the PM-YASASVI (Prime Minister Young Achievers…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Educational Opportunities for OBC, EBC and DNT Students through PM-YASASVI
PM-YASASVI Umbrella Scheme Provides Scholarship Support from Pre-Matric to Higher Education
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding educational opportunities for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC), Economically Backward Classes (EBC) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT) through the PM-YASASVI (Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India) umbrella scheme. The scheme aims to reduce financial barriers and promote inclusive, equitable and quality education for eligible students from these communities.

This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in a written reply to Member of Parliament Shri Kamakhya Prasad Tasa in Lok Sabha.

The House was informed that the PM-YASASVI umbrella scheme comprises of four major scholarship components designed to support students at different stages of education. These include the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Top Class Education in Schools Scheme, and Top Class Education in Colleges Scheme for eligible students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT communities.

The written reply further stated that the PM-YASASVI scheme is specifically intended to provide financial assistance to eligible students from these identified beneficiary groups, enabling them to pursue school and higher education without financial hardship.

The scheme is an important step towards ensuring that socially and educationally disadvantaged communities receive greater access to quality education and equal opportunities.

item.title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has put in place well-defined mechanisms to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
item.description: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has put in place well-defined mechanisms to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has put in place well-defined mechanisms to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics. Important mechanisms which are in place to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics are outlined below. Primary data…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has put in place well-defined mechanisms to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has put in place well-defined mechanisms to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics. Important mechanisms which are in place to ensure timely collection and publication of official statistics are outlined below.

Primary data collection for National Sample Surveys (NSS) are carried out on digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) and the e-SIGMA system, incorporating in-built validation checks, real-time data monitoring, AI-enabled chatbots, and multilingual interfaces. Use of such digital platforms ensure consistency at the stage of data collection and facilitate real-time submission and validation of survey data. Further, the practice of physical scrutiny and inspection by higher-level officers is continuously undertaken as per fixed norms along with regular training for field staff to ensure the quality of the data collected. These initiatives have substantially improved data quality and led to reduction in time lag in release of survey data from 8-9 months to 45-90 days. Annual Survey Results are now released within 90-120 days; quarterly results within 45-60 days and monthly results within 15-30 days of completion of surveys.

Similarly, the price data for the Consumer Price Index (CPI) are collected through the CAPI system under the new CPI series (Base Year 2024), incorporating real-time validation checks, geo-tagging and time-stamping of observations to strengthen data quality, monitoring, transparency and timeliness. Likewise, the estimates of National Accounts Statistics (NAS) are compiled and revised in accordance with the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008), using the latest available data sourced from various administrative databases and sample surveys. Similarly, adequate mechanism are in place to ensure timely collection and publication of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP). Monthly data is collected from data sources by 21st day of every month. Regular follow-up is undertaken to improve timeliness and response rates. For the compilation of IIP, data are subjected to validation and consistency checks to ensure their quality and reliability.

Further, MoSPI enhances accountability and ensures timely dissemination of statistical products/ publications through the Advance Release Calendar (ARC), which is placed on the Ministry's website and followed for the release of official statistical publications.

To promote transparency and public accountability, anonymized unit-level survey data are made available through MoSPI’s revamped Microdata Portal, enabling researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders to access, analyze, and utilize official statistics for evidence-based research and policy making.

MoSPI has also strengthened stakeholder engagement through data user conferences, consultations, workshops and feedback mechanisms, while digital platforms such as the revamped MoSPI website, GoIStats mobile application, e-Sankhyiki Portal, Microdata Portal and APIs for data exchange have enhanced data accessibility and dissemination

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Lok Sabha today.                   

                                                           ***

item.title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation undertakes periodic methodological reviews of statistical framework to ensure oﬃcial statistics remain representative of current structure of economy
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
item.description: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation undertakes periodic methodological reviews of statistical framework to ensure oﬃcial statistics remain representative of current structure of economy Modernization of National Sample Surveys has been done through various initiatives such as adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview and e-SIGMA system Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) undertakes periodic…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation undertakes periodic methodological reviews of statistical framework to ensure oﬃcial statistics remain representative of current structure of economy
Modernization of National Sample Surveys has been done through various initiatives such as adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview and e-SIGMA system
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) undertakes periodic methodological reviews of the statistical framework to ensure that oﬃcial statistics remain representative of the current structure of the economy and continue to meet emerging data requirements. The major methodological reviews undertaken by the Ministry are outlined below.

MoSPI has undertaken comprehensive base revision exercises for the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), All India Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) to ensure that these macroeconomic indicators adequately reflect the evolving structure of the economy and align with international statistical standards. Accordingly, the base year of GDP has been revised from 2011–12 to 2022–23 based on the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS); the base year of IIP has been revised from 2011–12 to 2022–23 under the guidance of the Technical Advisory Committee on IIP; and the base year of CPI has been revised from 2012=100 to 2024=100 under the guidance of an Expert Group constituted for the purpose. These revisions incorporate updated data sources, expanded coverage, revised item baskets and weights, improved estimation methodologies, enhanced use of administrative data sources such as GST and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) database, improved estimation of the unincorporated sector using the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), adoption of internationally accepted statistical practices, and other methodological refinements.

In addition, many technical consultations and brainstorming sessions were held with experts, academicians, State Governments and other stakeholders for seeking their inputs and feedback for base revision exercise of aforementioned macro economic indicators. Moreover, pre-release consultative workshops were also held before the release of the revised series of these indicators.

Further, MoSPI continuously reviews and updates the statistical standards, concepts, classiﬁcations, survey instruments and methodologies adopted in National Sample Surveys (NSS) to meet emerging data requirements, align with national and international best practices, and improve the quality, relevance and timeliness of oﬃcial statistics. Accordingly, survey schedules/questionnaires, sampling design, concepts and deﬁnitions, item classiﬁcations, ﬁeld procedures, data collection methodology, validation protocols and tabulation plans are reviewed before each major survey based on recommendations of the Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys (NSS), Technical Advisory Groups (TAGs), survey-speciﬁc Technical Expert Groups(TEGs), and consultations with Central Ministries/Departments, State Governments, subject matter experts and other stakeholders. The changes are ﬁnalized after pilot studies and ﬁeld testing, wherever required.

As a result, modernization of National Sample Surveys has been done through various initiatives such as the adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) and the e-SIGMA system, incorporating in-built validation checks, real-time data monitoring, AI-enabled chatbots, and multilingual interfaces. These initiatives have substantially improved data quality and led to reduction in time lag in release of survey data from 8-9 months to 45-90 days. Annual Survey Results are now released within 90-120 days; quarterly results within 45-60 days and monthly results within 15-30 days of completion of surveys. MoSPI has launched short duration surveys to cater the emerging need for high-frequency socio-economic indicators. Additionally, sampling design of major surveys have been modiﬁed by adopting district as the basic stratum enabling states to generate district level estimates of key indicators.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
ENERGY STATISTICS INDIA
Total Primary Energy Supply of India during 2024-25 was estimated at 39,055 Petajoules as compared to 37,936 Petajoules in 2023-24
Total Renewable Energy Potential as on 31-Mar-25 was estimated at 4,704,043 MW as compared to 2,109,655 MW as on 31-Mar-24
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi

In the 33rd edition of Energy Statistics 2026, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has, inter-alia made the following improvements:

  1. Inclusion of statistics on ‘Credit flow to energy-sector’,  ‘International energy scenario’ and ‘international marine and aviation bunker’ data;
  2. Alignment of end-use consuming sectors of all the energy-commodities with International standards;
  • iii. Addressing data-gaps on industry-wise consumption of Coal and Electricity.

 The Total Primary Energy Supply (TPES) of India during 2024-25 was estimated at 39,055 Petajoules as compared to 37,936 Petajoules in 2023-24. Total Renewable Energy Potential as on 31-Mar-25 was estimated at 4,704,043 MW as compared to 2,109,655 MW as on 31-Mar-24.

The publication “Energy Statistics India 2026” is widely disseminated among the users and all line-energy Ministries for policy and infrastructure planning. The publication is shared with all the States/UTs for taking suitable policy intervention. The publication is also available in public domain on the website of the Ministry for research and analysis by other users and stakeholders.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of

Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of  Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
NeVA Sewa Kendras have been established in 22 Legislative Houses
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi

As of now, National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) Sewa Kendras (e-Facilitation Centres) have been established in 22 Legislative Houses.

Under the Capacity Building component of the NeVA project, comprehensive orientation workshops and handholding support are provided to stakeholders of all on boarded Legislatures to familiarize them with the functionalities of NeVA. Recently, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs delivered a session on NeVA to the newly elected Members of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly at Kolkata on 04.07.2026.

The NeVA Public Portal, available in 23 languages, provides citizens with online access to legislative business, including Bills, Questions, Proceedings and other legislative documents of Legislatures on boarded on the NeVA platform. As such, having multilingual support, the portal is being widely used by the public to access legislative information.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of Law and Justice and Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Earthquake Risk in Kangra-Chamba-Dharamsala Belt
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken note of the seismic activity in the Kangra–Chamba region. The National Center for Seismology (NCS) under Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) continuously monitors earthquakes across the country through the National Seismological Network.  During June 2026, a total of 16 earthquakes were detected and reported by NCS through its 24×7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre in the Kangra–Chamba region of Himachal Pradesh, as against 18 mentioned in the question. Magnitude-wise details of these earthquakes are as follows:

Magnitude Range

2.0 - 2.9

3.0 - 3.9

4.0 - 4.9

5.0 - 5.9

No. of Earthquakes

12

3

NIL

1

 

The Kangra–Chamba–Dharamshala region lies in Seismic Zone V, the highest earthquake hazard zone in India. Scientific studies, including those by NGRI and other institutions, indicate that the region is capable of generating large earthquakes exceeding magnitude 7.0 due to active tectonic processes.

The Government has strengthened earthquake monitoring by expanding the National Seismological Network and ensuring round-the-clock monitoring by NCS. Presently, NCS maintains the National Seismological Network of 172 seismic stations across the country for 24×7 real time earthquake monitoring. Out of 172, 7 stations (Shimla, Dharamshala, Tissa, Sundernagar, Kalpa, Bhakra and Pong Dam) are in Himachal Pradesh. In addition, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), in coordination with State Governments, promotes earthquake preparedness through mock drills, training of officials and first responders, preparation of disaster management plans, and strengthening of emergency response mechanisms.

The Government has issued advisories and guidelines for adoption and enforcement of earthquake-resistant construction through the National Building Code (NBC), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) seismic design codes and Model Building Bye-Laws. The implementation of these codes is the responsibility of the respective State Governments and Urban Local Bodies.

The Government follows a strategy to minimize loss of life and property through risk assessment, preparedness, capacity building, strengthening of critical infrastructures and promotion of retrofitting of vulnerable lifeline buildings by the concerned authorities. NDMA regularly undertakes public awareness campaigns, conducts school and community awareness programmes, mock exercises and training programmes to promote earthquake safety and preparedness.

Seismic microzonation studies are undertaken by scientific institutions and universities. The Government continues to provide financial and technical assistance to states, including Himachal Pradesh, under various disaster management and mitigation schemes to enhance disaster resilience and preparedness.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

The objective of Mission Mausam is to strengthen various components of the Earth System observations, to realize Earth System approach to provide an early warning system, for seamless weather and climate services to all. The scheme seeks to exponentially enhance the country's weather and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPLEMENTATION OF MISSION MAUSAM
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Mission Mausam was launched by the Honorable Prime Minister on 14 January 2025 with the goal of making country a 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart' nation. The objective of Mission Mausam is to strengthen various components of the Earth System observations, to realize Earth System approach to provide an early warning system, for seamless weather and climate services to all. The scheme seeks to exponentially enhance the country's weather and climate observations, understanding, modelling and forecasting, leading to better, more useful, accurate, and timely services. The key objectives of this Mission include:

  • Developing cutting-edge weather surveillance technologies and systems.
  • Implementing higher-resolution atmospheric observations with improved temporal and spatial sampling and coverage.
  • Deploying next-generation  radars, wind profilers, and satellites equipped with advanced instrument payloads.
  • Implementing advanced high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
  • Enhancing our understanding of weather and climate processes and improving prediction capabilities.
  • Developing advanced Earth system models and data-driven methods, including the use of AI/ML.
  • Creating technologies and protocols for effective weather management.
  • Establishing a state-of-the-art Decision Support System (DSS) and dissemination system for last-mile connectivity.
  • Strengthening capacity building and research collaborations.

The current status of the observational network and modeling capability are as follows:

  • India Meteorological Department (IMD) presently receives data from a network of 50 Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs) operated by IMD and other MoES institutions and ISRO across the country. The present network shall be augmented through ongoing projects with the deployment of 29 C-Band DWRs, 45 X-Band DWRs and 12 S-Band DWRs throughout the country.
  • Under the project, various global and regional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) modeling systems have been implemented and operationalize to generate seamlessly short range, medium range and extended range forecasts. There are two different framework of global modeling systems based on global forecast systems (GFS) of IMD and Mithuna modeling systems of NCMRWF Noida. Both the models run on real time with horizontal resolution 12 KM. The New Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS) operational at a very high resolution of 6 km to cater to block levels and further to panchayat levels. In order to provide computational support of such high resolution models and to make it regularly run in real time, the Computing facilities also has been substantially increased with computational power to integrate voluminous data and to run mesoscale, regional and global models at higher resolution. Recently, with "Arunika" and "Arka" systems, the Ministry of Earth Sciences has enhanced its total computing power to 28 Peta FLOPS in 2025, a substantial increase from the previous capacity of 6.8 Peta FLOPS which was in 2014.
  • Currently three AI based global models are regularly operational to provide guidance to the forecaster to predict severe weather. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications and tools have been developed indigenously by weather scientist of MoES organization on various aspects of monitoring and observational processing such as Nowcasting tool, downscaled urban forecasting etc. 

Various initiatives were taken by IMD for the improvement of disaster early warning systems. The important majors taken are as follows:

  • Augmentation of observational network.
  • Development of indigenous, technology-driven, and citizen-centric weather forecasting systems that strengthen disaster preparedness and improve public safety across India (Points 2 & 3 above). IMD's in house developed Decision Support System (DSS) is a major step in the direction of promoting self-reliance under the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative. As a result, there is 40% improvement in forecast accuracy for all type of severe weather events in recent decades as compared to previous decade.
  • Impact-based forecasts and risk-based warnings are being disseminated at the district level, empowering authorities to take timely preventive actions against cyclones, heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, heatwaves, and cold waves.
  • Developed "Mausamgram" (Har Har Mausam, Har Ghar Mausam) a unique citizen-focused platform providing location-specific, hyperlocal weather forecasts down to the village level. "Mausamgram" delivers hourly forecasts for the next 36 hours, three-hourly forecasts for the next five days, and six-hourly forecasts for up to ten days. Users can conveniently access weather information by searching through PIN code or location name, or by selecting the state, district, block, and gram panchayat. This user-friendly system ensures easy access to hyperlocal forecasts, enabling citizens to obtain accurate and timely weather updates tailored to their specific location.
  • Development of climate hazard and vulnerability maps at district level (https://imdpune.gov.in/hazardatlas/index.html)
  • Development of geospatial services for weather forecast and warnings (https://imdgeospatial.imd.gov.in/)
  • IMD is one of the agencies that generate CAP alerts for severe weather warnings. These CAP alerts are disseminated through SMS as well as the SACHET app, developed by the NDMA. These CAP feeds are also being used by APPLE, GOOGLE and GMAS for the dissemination of weather-related warnings. IMD has developed an Application Programming Interface (API) which is being used by various private and public organisations for further dissemination of IMD's forecasts and warnings to the general public through different media including mobile apps developed by different stakeholders.

 

  • IMD has developed various mobile apps for the dissemination of weather-related warnings such as MAUSAM App for weather forecasting and warnings, MEGHDOOT App for agro met services, DAMINI App (developed by IITM) for lighting warning, UMANG App (developed by Meity) for Weather forecasting and warnings.

To ensure localised relevance and last-mile connectivity of weather updates in remote and vulnerable regions, IMD, in collaboration with other ministries, has undertaken the following major initiatives:

  • In collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, IMD has developed the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, providing Panchayat-level weather forecasts through e-GramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat App, e-Manchitra and Mausamgram (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in).
  • The mobile numbers of Panchayat Members, Ward Members and Panchayat Secretaries have been integrated with the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, enabling timely dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories through WhatsApp for further dissemination at the Gram Panchayat level.
  • IMD also leverages the Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis network of the Ministry of Rural Development for last-mile dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories.
  • IMD has organized over 7,300 Farmers' Awareness Programmes (FAPs) across 373 districts, benefiting nearly 3.67 lakh farmers, including 83 Aspirational Districts, to promote climate-resilient agriculture and the effective use of weather-based advisory services.
  • Under Mission Mausam, IMD has developed KALP (Krishi Advisory based on Location-specific Weather Prediction) for generation of location-, crop- and crop-stage-specific advisories and Mausam SANKALP (Systematic Agrometeorological aNalytics, Knowledge and Advisory enabLing Platform) to strengthen weather analytics, advisory generation and climate-resilient agricultural planning.

Government of India through MoES institutions and IMD has undertaken continuous monitoring & rigorous review of operational meteorological services covering all temporal and spatial scales in seamless manner. There has been significant progress in modernising the national, regional and local meteorological early-warning system in recent past with implementation of Multi-Hazard Early Warning System of IMD with state of art suit of GIS enabled Decision Support System with objective of "No Weather should go Undetected and Unpredicted". To meet primary objective of the goal, meteorological observational infrastructure in Uttar Pradesh is being strengthened continuously under the Urban Meteorology and Mission Mausam schemes of Government of India to fill the observational gaps comprehensively with multilateral approach though Mission Mausam to increase the preparedness and effectiveness of disaster risk reduction measures for various desired targeted vulnerable groups/communities of the state including major agricultural areas like Meerut and Hapur districts of Uttar Pradesh in close co-operation with the local/state government allied departments & agencies to address the multilateral impacts & challenges offered due to severe weather hazards thunderstorms, hailstorms, heavy rainfall etc.

Furthermore, numerous efforts have been undertaken by the Government of India through IMD and other MoES institutions to strengthen climate resilience through effective early warning system, heat-action plan, sectoral disaster management plans and district-level preparedness. As an effective initiative to monitor and track the extreme weather and climate events such as heat waves, thunderstorms, extreme rainfall and floods for the state of Uttar Pradesh and to improve disaster preparedness and weather forecasting of the state recently IMD, GoI and GoUP has taken joint initiative and signed an MoU for enhancing the existing observational network. A network of 29 automated instruments (05-AWS + 24-ARG) in district Meerut and that of 13 automated instruments (03-AWS + 10-ARG) in district Hapur (all quipped with temperature, humidity and rainfall sensors) has already been established and commissioned in addition to the pre-existing IMD network of 01 Departmental Observatory at CCSU (Ramgarhi), 01 Agromet Observatory at SVPUAT (Modipuram), 04 DRMS stations (Meerut Tehsil, Meerot Observatory, Sardhana & Mawana) and 03 automated instruments (01-AWS-CCSU + 02-ARG-Sardhana & Mawana) in Meerut district and 02 DRMS stations (Garhmukteshwar & Hapur)  in Hapur district. Apart from the aforesaid network there is an existing robust network of 3 Doppler Weather Radars in Delhi (Aya Nagar, Plam & Lodhi Road) and 01 each in Patiala and Lansdown to cater the needs of monitoring and forecast of severe weather elements like Thunderstorms, Lightning, Hailstorm, Intense Rainfall Episodes and related Hazard of Northwest Uttar Pradesh including Meerut and Hapur.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: HEATWAVE FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNING SYSTEMS AT THE DISTRICT LEVEL
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:13PM by PIB Delhi

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), issues warnings and alerts, including impact-based forecasts (IBFs) for heatwaves, at the district level twice a day. It includes the expected impact and suggested actions to mitigate heatwaves, as outlined in the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines and the heat action plan. These impact-based forecasts and risk-based warnings at the district level are disseminated to disaster managers, stakeholders, the media, and the general public through multiple communication channels, including email, APIs, mobile applications, social media platforms, websites, electronic and print media, mass communication systems, and Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)-based dissemination mechanisms.

IMD has developed the Hazard and Vulnerability Atlas of India, which provides district-wise vulnerability assessments for heatwave hazards (https://imdpune.gov.in/hazardatlas/index.html). The Atlas covers all districts of the country, including Barmer district in Rajasthan. As per the Atlas, Barmer district has a Heatwave Vulnerability Index of 0.54 on a scale of 0 to 1, placing it in the High Vulnerability category.

IMD is sharing its heatwave bulletins with different stakeholders, including Disaster Management Authorities, Health Departments, Labour Departments, Indian Railways, Transport Department, Forest Departments, etc, on a regular basis. Further, IMD shares heatwave warnings with the general public through Websites, Mass Media, Social Media, WhatsApp groups, Mobile Apps, APIs, Common Alert Protocols, etc. As a pilot initiative, IMD initiated the dissemination of impact-based heatwave warnings to informal workers through their respective associations in a simple, easy-to-understand, and actionable format. Regular meetings are also held by the NDMA with various stakeholders to disseminate the IMD forecast for anticipatory and on-the-ground actions. Most of the heat wave-related products are available on a web-GIS-based platform and are openly accessible to the general public (https://dss.imd.gov.in/dwr_img/GIS/heatwave.html).

The Government has significantly strengthened heatwave monitoring, forecasting, and early warning systems through the India Meteorological Department in collaboration with the NDMA, State agencies, and local health departments. Heat Action Plans have been implemented in many parts of the country to provide advance warnings and guidance on preventive measures. Since 2016, IMD has issued seasonal outlooks for temperatures and heatwaves to support planning, along with monthly outlooks, extended-range (weekly) forecasts, and twice-daily heatwave bulletins for the public, disaster managers, and other stakeholders.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RAINFALL DEFICIT
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi

India Meteorological Department (IMD) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences monitors rainfall on a daily, weekly and seasonal basis against the Long Period Average (LPA). The Southwest Monsoon rainfall in 2026 has been lower than normal in several parts of the country during the initial weeks of the season. However, rainfall varies from place to place and from week to week, and some regions have received normal or above-normal rainfall. As of 14 July 2026, the country received 21% below normal rainfall, with several meteorological subdivisions recording deficient rainfall while others experienced normal or excess rainfall due to the natural variability of the Southwest Monsoon.

The impact of rainfall on agriculture, water resources, drinking water and groundwater is assessed by the concerned Ministries and State Governments. At present, there is no indication of any nationwide impact on food grain production.

Monsoon rainfall over India is inherently characterized by spatial and temporal variability, which can result in localized deficits or excess rainfall across different regions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) continuously monitors rainfall distribution and provides regular weather forecasts and warnings to assist administrative authorities in taking necessary operational measures. The assessment and declaration of drought or flood situations fall within the purview of the respective State Governments in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Government is strengthening weather forecasting through the Ministry of Earth Sciences' flagship programme, Mission Mausam. The mission aims to improve weather observations, gain a better understanding of various physical processes, and develop advanced numerical models that incorporate these processes to improve the ability to forecast weather accurately.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: BHARAT FORECAST SYSTEM
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Bharat Forecast System (BharatFS) is based on the newly implemented Triangular Cubic Octahedral (TCo) dynamical grid that enables the model to operate at 6 km horizontal resolution, surpassing its predecessor (GFS T1534 ~ 12km) and typical global operational models having horizontal resolution of 9–14 km. The recently acquired supercomputing facilities, Arka (IITM-Pune) and Arunika (NCMRWF-Noida), enabled the model to be used for real-time weather prediction by reducing the runtime. These key features have enhanced India's weather prediction capabilities by making India the only country running a global weather prediction model at a high resolution of 6 km for real-time weather prediction. The BharatFS was developed with the objective of generating forecasts at the cluster of panchayats level and improving the prediction of extremes. 

With the increase in horizontal resolution, the BharatFS is capable of generating forecasts every 6 km. This allows the capturing of local weather features, thus enabling the forecasts to cater to a cluster of panchayats/villages. Localized forecasts help farmers with crop planning, irrigation, and harvesting. Additionally, water authorities can better manage reservoirs during monsoons, reducing flood risk and improving yield resilience. Climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of extreme events, and BharatFS has demonstrated significant improvement in the skill of predicting the core monsoon region's extreme rainfall. All these improvements are crucial for faster and targeted disaster response, increasing the disaster preparedness of our country.           

The BharatFS being developed indigenously is highly significant, not only for advancing India's scientific capabilities but also for furthering national strategic and economic goals. BharatFS represents India's own high-resolution weather prediction model, designed by Indian scientists considering the complexities of forecasting due to Indian geography—the Himalayas and Western Ghats.

The BharatFS was developed by a team of scientists from Indian institutions like IITM-Pune, with support from the NCMRWF-Noida and the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The modeling system is powered by indigenous MoES supercomputing facilities (Arka and Arunika). These achievements are aligned with "Make in India" – Showcasing India's capability to build world-class weather and climate forecasting systems locally. The development and launch of BharatFS has enabled India to upgrade its meteorological services and support neighboring countries, reinforcing regional leadership and self-reliance.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Blue Economy of Odisha under PMMSY
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India, has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) across all States and Union Territories, including Odisha, since 2020–21. During this period, the Department has approved fisheries development proposals submitted by the Government of Odisha, amounting to ₹1,301.18 crore, including a Central share of ₹484.64 crore, covering a wide range of interventions to strengthen the fisheries and aquaculture value chain. Under PMMSY, DoF, GoI, accorded approval in January 2025 for the establishment of the Integrated Aqua Park at Basantapur, Sambalpur with a project cost of ₹100 crore. As reported by the State Government, key preparatory works such as land procurement, issuance of the letter of intent to the executing agency, and construction of the approach road and boundary walls, have been completed. Construction of the in‑house hatchery facility, grow‑out ponds, processing units, research facilities and the effluent treatment plant are at various stage.

(b)       The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India, under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), has also approved the construction of the State of Art Wholesale Fish Market at Pandara, Bhubaneswar, at a total project cost of ₹59.13 crore, comprising 44 wholesale units and 99 retail units. The market is designed with modern sustainability features, including a renewable‑energy‑based power system and rainwater harvesting infrastructure, aimed at reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and improving resource efficiency. As reported by the Government of Odisha, land reclamation stage has been completed.

(c) and (d) The Government of India has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish farmers since FY 2018‑19, thereby ensuring timely and affordable working capital for fisheries‑related activities. The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, in collaboration with the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, is actively engaging with all States/UTs and the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) to raise awareness and disseminate information among fishers and fish farmers for availing KCC benefits.

As per the Government of Odisha, the State Government conducts regular awareness programmes through Matsya O Pranee Sampad Melas and fishermen meetings at the district, block, and village levels to enhance uptake of the scheme. Further, the State Government provides an additional interest subvention of 4% for loans up to ₹1.00 lakh and 2% for loans above ₹1.00 lakh and up to ₹3.00 lakh. This makes KCC loans interest‑free up to ₹1.00 lakh and reduces the effective interest rate to 2% for loans between ₹1.00 lakh and ₹3.00 lakh, thereby significantly improving credit affordability for beneficiaries.

 This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Welfare of shrimp farmer
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  has taken up several initiatives for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture in the country including implementation of various schemes such as (i) Centrally Sponsored Scheme on Blue Revolution : Integrated Development and Management of Fisheries implemented for a period of 5 years from FY2015-16 to FY2019-20, (ii)  Fisheries&Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) implemented with effect from year 2018-19, (iii) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and (iv)  Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY). Additionally, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018-19 has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirements. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during the last 3 years financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) has accorded approvals to the fisheries and aquaculture development proposals of various State Governments and Union Territories (UTs) at a total cost of Rs.6,885.18 crore with central share of Rs.3,159.83 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).  The central funds of Rs.2,208.74 crore has been released during the last three years (2023-24 to 2025-26) to the State Governments and UTs for implementation of various approved fisheries and aquaculture development projects under PMMSY. State/UT-wise details of the proposals approved and central funds released during the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) under PMMSY are furnished at Annexure-I.

(c) and (d) :     To address the challenges of rising input costs, disease outbreaks and fluctuations in international market prices, the Government of India has been implementing measures several measures such as promotion of biosecurity, disease surveillance and diagnostics, dissemination of best management practices, and capacity building of fish farmers. Under the National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD) implemented under PMMSY, regular surveillance, early detection, reporting, and monitoring of aquatic animal diseases are undertaken to facilitate timely disease management and minimize production losses. Further, under PMMSY financial assistance has also been provided for establishment and strengthening of aquatic animal health infrastructure, disease diagnostic laboratories, hatcheries, and other interventions aimed at improving the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of the shrimp farming sector.

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India under the Pradhan Mantri,Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) inter-alia provides social security to fishers through group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre& State in the ratio of 60:40 basis, 90:10 for the Himalayan&North Eastern States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre. The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/- for permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs.25,000/.  During the last three years (2023-24 to 2025-26), the Department of Fisheries has released a sum of Rs.54.03 crore for insurance coverage of 103.73 lakh fishers with an average of 34.57 lakh fishers annually.

In addition, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) also provides one time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by farmers. The insurance products available under this scheme includes: (i) Basic Insurance which covers yield losses due to non-preventable perils(risks), such as summer kill, pollution, earthquakes, cyclones, floods, other natural calamities, riots, malicious acts of third parties including poisoning, loss of crop due to structural damage of farms and (ii) Comprehensive Insurance which covers perils under Basic Insurance and additional perils due to diseases etc. The one time incentive for aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1lakh per farmer for 4 hectares Water Spread Area (WSA). For the aquaculture system including intensive systems like farms, cage culture, RAS, bio-floc, and raceways etc., aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹1 lakh per farmer for 1800 m3 for intensive aquaculture systems. Further, the SC/ST and women beneficiaries are provided an additional 10% of incentive.

Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Development of cold water fisheries
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing a flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with an  investment of Rs 20,050 crore in all the States/Union Territories. In order to address the infrastructure gaps in fisheries and  aquaculture, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India with effect  from the financial year 2018-19 has also been implementing a dedicated fund Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) with a fund size of Rs 7522.48 crore.

 

The PMMSY inter alia aims to address critical gaps in fish production and productivity, quality, technology, post-harvest infrastructure and management, modernisation and strengthening of value chain, traceability, establishing a robust fisheries management framework and fishers’ welfare in cold water fisheries.

 

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has approved  various fisheries developmental projects of Himalayan and Hilly States for an amount of Rs.706 crore including projects for cold water fisheries development. A framework titled Model Guidelines for the Development of Cold Water Fisheries was issued on 14th March, 2026 to support States in developing coldwater fisheries and its associated infrastructure. These guidelines provide specifications for development of Raceways, Re-circulatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), hatcheries, feed mills, disease prevention and market linkagesfor augmenting production, value addition and marketing of commercially important coldwater fish species like Rainbow Trout, Golden Mahseer and Snow Trout. In addition, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has notified four clusters specifically for development of cold water fisheries at  Anant Nag District in Jammu and Kashmir,  Pithoragarh District in Uttarakhand,  Kargil District in Ladakh and  Kullu District in Himachal Pradesh.

 

(c) and (d) : The Department of Fisheries, Government of India promotes adoption of emerging technologies such as RAS, Biofloc, Cages, IoT‑based water quality monitoring, GIS mapping, automated feeders and digital market platforms for  fish farmers in remote and mountainous regions. Under PMMSY, a model RAS for coldwater fisheries has been developed through Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)-Central Institute of Coldwater Fisheries Research (ICAR-CICFR), Bhimtal for intensive trout production and year‑round breeding of Golden Mahseer. Moreover, ICAR‑Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (CIFT) Kochi has supported fish processing and Ready‑to‑Eat facilities in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

 

This Information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Allocation of funds under Blue Revolution
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 has been implementing a flagship scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country. The State/UT-wise details of fund approved and released under the PMMSY during the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) is furnished at Annexure-I. The State/UT-wise allocation of central funds under PMMSY are made on annual basis depending on the overall budgetary allocation, performance of the States/UTs, fund absorbing capacity, physical and financial progress,  liabilities created in respect of the projects approved in the previous financial years. There is no disparity in allocation of funds among the States and Union Territories under the PMMSY. The fisheries and aquaculture development projects and initiatives taken by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India under the PMMSY have contributed towards augmentation of fish production, productivity and exports. During the last five years (2020-21 to 2024-25), fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 lakh tonne in 2019-20 to 197.75 lakh tonne in 2024-25 (39.61% increase) and fisheries export from Rs.46,666 crore (2019-20) to Rs.73,890 crore (2025-26) (58.34% increase). The Department of Fisheries has developed the PMMSY Management Information System (MIS) as a centralized digital portal and dashboard utilized to track the progress of the Fisheries projects taken up under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The MIS aggregates district and state-level data to enable monitoring and evaluation of the progress. Issuance of need based advisories, regular physical and virtual meetings with the States/UTs and field visits are undertaken to monitor and review the progress of projects and improve the effective utilization of funds.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Women led cooperatives in fisheries
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) supports the formation of Fisheries Cooperative Societies across the country including in the state of Andhra Pradesh.  The Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that a total of 213 women-led coastal Cooperative Societies have been formed in the areas of fisheries, seaweed cultivation and marine processing, benefitting 27,447 beneficiaries across 12 districts, including Kakinada from 1st April 2021 to 15th June 2026 . The district wise details of women-led coastal cooperative societies along with the number of beneficiaries associated with them, are given at Annexure-I.  

(c) For the promotion and strengthening of women-led coastal fisheries cooperatives across the country, the Government of India is continuously engaging with the States and Union Territories through various schemes and programmes. As part of these efforts, fisheries cooperatives are encouraged to register on the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) and are eligible for higher incentives, including performance grants of up to ₹2 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PMMKSSY). Women-led fisheries cooperatives are also accorded priority in the issuance of Access Passes for fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Letters of Authorization (LoA) for High Seas fishing. Further, to facilitate greater participation of fisheries cooperatives in High Seas fishing, the application and renewal fee for the Letter of Authorization has been reduced from ₹25,000 to ₹5,000.

(d) As a part of Blue Economy, the Department of Fisheries, through National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), has formulated an action plan to support the formation of 12,000 fisheries cooperatives across the country, including women-led Coastal Cooperative Societies in uncovered panchayats and villages. In addition, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Saha-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) a sub-scheme of PMMSY envisages for strengthening of 5500 Primary Fisheries Cooperative Societies across the country including women-led Fisheries Cooperative Societies, with mentoring, capacity building and need based financial support.

Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Blue Economy through reservoir and Amrit Sarovar fisheries
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihood of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for development of fisheries in Amrit Sarovars and Reservoirs.

(b): The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars will be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The selection has been done in consultation with the States and UTs, considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. State and UT wise reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars identified as on date are at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively.

(c): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fisher’s income in the country is promoting Fish Farmer Producer Organization (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of new Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Traceability systems in seafood export
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, is implementing several strategic initiatives to strengthen seafood export infrastructure under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Under PMMSY, projects for the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector, amounting to ₹21,394.88 crore with a Central share of ₹9,510.89 crore, have been approved, including those for the creation and strengthening of export infrastructure. Further, infrastructure has been augmented through the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), under which 18 major projects, with a total project cost of ₹345.89 crore, have been supported, primarily for the expansion and modernization of fish processing plants. The year-wise and State-wise details of financial assistance provided under PMMSY and FIDF are enclosed at Annexure-II and Annexure-III, respectively. In addition, the MPEDA is implementing the Technology Development for Specific Value-Added Marine Products (TDSVMP) Scheme, under which financial assistance is provided for the development of value-added infrastructure. The Scheme supports the establishment and modernization of fish processing facilities, cold storage, automated processing machinery, infrastructure for handling live, chilled, ornamental, and dried fish, and the development of new value-added seafood products. During the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, MPEDA has provided financial assistance of ₹118.10 crore to 89 seafood processing units for infrastructure development under the Scheme.

 

  1. The Export Inspection Council (EIC), under the Department of Commerce, is the Competent Authority for quality control and inspection of notified export products, including marine products. To ensure compliance with importing countries' requirements, EIC conducts periodic training on Food Safety Management System (FSMS) requirements for approved seafood export establishments and mandates testing of aquaculture shrimp for banned antibiotics during export certification. The MPEDA supports these efforts through pre-harvest testing, certification programmes such as SHAPHARI, and, together with the Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA) and EIC, implementing the National Residue Control Plan (NRCP) to strengthen residue monitoring, traceability, and compliance with international standards. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, supports quality enhancement and export competitiveness through the PMMSY by promoting branding, standards and certification, capacity building, post-harvest infrastructure, cold-chain facilities, and the modernization of fishing harbours and fish landing centres. The Department of Fisheries, GoIalso supports the culture of export-oriented species such as Scampi, Mud Crab, Asian Seabass, and Cobia, and promotes advanced aquaculture technologies, including Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc technology. Further, the Department of Fisheries, GoI is promoting sustainable seafood production by supporting the Marine Mammal Stock Assessment Project and the fitment of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) on shrimp trawls under PMMSY. In addition, the CAA has updated the list of prohibited pharmacologically active substances and antimicrobial agents under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Rules, 2024, to strengthen compliance with international food safety requirements.

 

  1. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has released the National Framework on Traceability in Fisheries and Aquaculture, 2025, to establish a national digital traceability system across the fisheries and aquaculture value chain. The Framework aims to ensure compliance with domestic and international requirements, strengthen food safety, quality assurance, and transparency, enhance consumer confidence, and facilitate market access, thereby boosting seafood exports. It envisages a phased and technology-driven implementation through a National Level Governance Committee (NLGC) for strategic oversight and an Adoption Committee to facilitate the adoption of an IT-based national traceability system by fisheries and aquaculture stakeholders.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Review of implementation of PMMSY
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), regularly reviews the implementation of projects approved under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in all States/Union Territories(UTs) including Maharashtra through physical meetings, virtual meetings, field visits and digital monitoring through a dedicated centralized digital platform for scheme implementation.

(b) and (c): Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), during 2020-21 to 2026-27, the DoF, GoI has approved the proposals for fisheries development submitted by the Government of Maharashtra amounting to Rs. 1,601.44 crore, with central share of Rs. 593.33 crore. Out of this, central funds amounting to Rs. 419.02 crore has been released and the Government of Maharashtra has utilized Rs. 408.77 crore of this released funds.

The approvals include various fisheries activities towards enhancing fish production, productivity, strengthening infrastructure facilities, development of cold chain and marketing facilities, sustainability of resources and activities towards fishermen safety and welfare. Under PMMSY, beneficiary selection and projects implementation are done by the respective State Governments/UTs. The district-wise details of important fisheries infrastructure projects implemented under PMMSY as reported by Government of Maharashtra are Annexed. 

(d): The Government of Maharashtra has informed total of 3714 beneficiary oriented projects are active in the State under PMMSY out of which 2856 projects are 100% completed. From these, direct employment for 15,763 persons and indirect employment opportunities for 19,528 persons are generated in the State. It is also informed that upon completion of all approved projects, the ongoing projects are expected to generate additional employment opportunities and further strengthen the socio-economic status of the fisheries sector in Maharashtra.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Fisheries, reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihood of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for development of fisheries in Amrit Sarovars and Reservoirs. The key components envisaged for implementation of such initiatives includes strengthening quality seed production by establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value added unit.

(b): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) in consultation with States and Union Territories (UTs) has selected 351 reservoirs and 100 Amrit Sarovars. The selection was based on the lists submitted by the States and UTs, considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars.

(c): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fisher’s income in the country is promoting Fish Farmer Producer Organization (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of new Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars.

(d): The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars shall be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The unit cost and funding pattern shall be as per the existing guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.
