item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
RURAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEMES
Posted On: 21 JUL 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

Under Budget Estimate (BE) 2026-27, Rs. 2,31,423.14 crore has been allocated to the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), of which Rs. 2,28,768.81 crore is for the Department of Rural Development. Allocation under BE is made against various programmes/schemes of the respective Departments but not State/UT-wise. Out of the allocation made for the programmes/ schemes under the budget estimate, funds are released to the States/Union Territories through respective implementing mechanisms of the schemes, which includes submission of requisite documents / utilization certificate as per schematic requirements ensuring proper utilization of funds already allocated under the schemes, ensuring strict adherence of the schematic guidelines, assessing the actual requirement at the ground level and taking into account the balance of funds available with the States.

National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) and the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) of MoRD are implemented in the UT of Delhi.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
REVISION OF AMOUNT UNDER NSAP
Posted On: 21 JUL 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is being implemented across the country as a social security programme, for vulnerable sections of the society such as old aged, widows and disabled persons belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL). The rate of Central assistance under NSAP pension schemes including National Old Age Pension Scheme, National Widow Pension Scheme and National Disability Pension Scheme was last revised in 2012.

NSAP caters to more than 3 crore BPL beneficiaries and as per the information collected from States/UTs, about 5.9 crore additional pensioners are supported by state-funded social pension schemes. Therefore, around 9 crore beneficiaries are receiving pension benefits either under Central pension schemes and/or under State-specific social security pension schemes, many of which have expanded coverage and higher assistance levels tailored to local needs. At present, States are giving top up amount to the beneficiaries ranging from ₹50/- to ₹5700/- per month. As a result, NSAP pensioners are getting monthly pension on an average of Rs. 1100/- in several States/ UTs. State/UT-wise details of top-up paid by the States/UTs are at Annexure.

From time to time, various impact assessment and evaluation studies have been carried out to assess the impact of NSAP schemes by the Ministry and NITI Aayog. The assessments indicate satisfactory implementation at the grassroots level, with most beneficiaries expressing overall satisfaction with the processes of selection, sanction, and disbursement of pensions. The studies also find that pension support has helped beneficiaries meet essential expenses such as food, healthcare, etc., thereby reducing their dependence on family members for these needs. At the same time, they have recommended further strengthening of the programme through measures such as improving adequacy of assistance, ensuring timely and regular payments, enhancing beneficiary verification and monitoring systems etc.

At present, there is no proposal under consideration to revise the rate of assistance under NSAP.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
VB-GRAM-G SCHEME
Posted On: 21 JUL 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi

All States and Union Territories have notified their respective State Schemes in compliance of the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM–G) Act, 2025. The implementation of the Scheme has commenced in rural areas of the entire country w.e.f. 01.07.2026. State/UT-wise details of funds allocated and released under the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM-G) since its commencement on 01.07.2026 is given at Annexure. However, since the scheme has been operationalized only on July 1st, 2026 utilization of the fund and release of payments will be done by the States after closer of Muster Rolls and subsequent FTO generation.

The Central Government has been continuously reviewing the preparedness of the States and Union Territories for successful implementation of the VB–G RAM–G. In addition to Weekly Review Meetings, several review meetings were held under the chairpersonship of Minister for Rural Development and Secretary, Rural Development. As an outcome of these review meetings, hand holding and technical support continuously provided by the Ministry,

all States/UTs have been able to successfully start the implementation of the scheme w.e.f. 01.07.2026.   The Ministry maintains continuous engagement with the States and Union Territories through regular review meetings, consultations and other appropriate fora to facilitate effective implementation of the Scheme. Suggestions given by States/UTs during various review meetings and written communication have duly been noted by the Ministry.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
